item.title: The UFO Origins Question Washington May Have to Answer
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: Sources have told Liberation Times that officials are weighing a public statement that some UAP involve non-human intelligence interacting with humanity, accompanied by the potential public rollout of retrieved exotic materials.
item.content:encoded:
• Sources tell Liberation Times that US officials are weighing a public statement acknowledging that some UAP involve non-human intelligence. They are also considering whether to reveal materials said to have been recovered.

  • Physicist and former Pentagon adviser Hal Puthoff explored four possible origins for some UAP, including the possibility that a hidden population has long lived on Earth.

  • Liberation Times understands that US intelligence and special operations personnel have been referred to Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory after alleged encounters. One source pointed to Z Division, the lab’s intelligence unit.

  • Sources describe alleged hostilities between some non-human groups and say attitudes towards humanity may range from benevolence to hostility. Former Pentagon official Lue Elizondo told Liberation Times there is no clear way to confirm their intentions.

  • UAP whistleblower David Grusch says he watched footage of a crash retrieval that showed several dead, human-looking figures. He described them as “very, very beautiful” and compared them to Greek gods.

Written by Christopher Sharp - 26 November 2026

Sources have told Liberation Times that officials are weighing a public statement that some UAP involve non-human intelligence interacting with humanity, accompanied by the potential public rollout of retrieved exotic materials. 

If such an event ever came to pass, it would undoubtedly raise two questions as consequential as the disclosure itself: where do they come from? What do they want?

In a 2022 paper, physicist and former Pentagon UAP adviser Hal Puthoff explored several possibilities, including one that challenges the usual assumption of visitors arriving from elsewhere in the universe: that some source of the phenomenon may already be on Earth.

Puthoff is no distant observer of the UAP debate, nor is he a person whose credentials can be scoffed at. 

His career includes research at the National Security Agency and SRI International, the Silicon Valley institute that developed the first computer mouse and helped lay the foundations of the internet. 

More recently, he had served as a senior science adviser and contractor to the U.S. Defence Department’s AAWSAP investigation into UAP. 

He had worked within the small circle of people tasked with studying the subject, seen as gatekeepers - the few who knew the truth behind the enigma of UAP. 

That circle included James Ryder - now deceased - a former vice-president of Lockheed Martin Space Systems and head of its Advanced Technology Center. In a recorded talk, Ryder called Puthoff his friend; a 2017 project document lists them on the same science review team. 

Jay Stratton, who led the U.S. Navy’s UAP Task Force, said Ryder had spoken to him about a legacy UAP program and Lockheed Martin’s alleged role in it.

Stratton claims Ryder told him that Lockheed Martin possessed twelve non-human vehicles.

Ryder’s name later surfaced in material submitted to Congress, which alleged that he had proposed transferring purported recovered UAP material from Lockheed Martin to AAWSAP, where Stratton and Puthoff both worked. 

Puthoff remains something of a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside an enigma. He weighs every word, as though a single unguarded remark could have profound consequences.

In a 2025 interview with Joe Rogan, Puthoff recalled attending a meeting in Northern Virginia around 2004, during George W. Bush’s presidency - something verified by the U.S. government’s UAP office, known as the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office.

Participants, he said, were asked to consider what would happen if the United States, Russia and China disclosed that they possessed crashed extraterrestrial craft and bodies. 

They weighed the potential effects on religion, financial markets, politics and defence companies. Puthoff said the group’s assessment was negative. 

More than 20 years later, a similar issue may now be before the White House, with sources telling Liberation Times that administration officials have a disclosure plan in place, which is currently being considered.

Due to his background and the people associated with him, such as Ryder, Puthoff’s paper from 2022 should be taken seriously.

In his paper, Puthoff considers four illustrative hypotheses regarding the origin of some UAP:

  • Extraterrestrials: visitors from another world, whose craft or biological remains might have been recovered and studied

  • Isolated humans: a technologically advanced human community that has developed apart from the rest of civilisation

  • Stranded or colonising extraterrestrials: beings who arrived long ago, remained on Earth and may have entered human accounts of gods or ancient civilisations

  • Interdimensional beings or time travellers: entities entering our world from another reality or another point in time.

Puthoff devotes particular attention to the middle two possibilities. He groups them under the term ultraterrestrials: a hidden population living on Earth, whether descended from humans or from visitors who settled here long ago. 

The persistence of reported sightings over decades, perhaps centuries, might suggest a nearby source, he argues. Reports that such beings express concern about nuclear weapons or environmental damage would also take on a different meaning if they shared the planet with us. 

Puthoff also refers to accounts from people who claimed they were abducted and taken to cave-like or undersea locations.

Why would they hide? Puthoff suggests that even a technologically superior population might fear exploitation, disease, assimilation or the loss of its culture. Secrecy, in his account, could involve more than concealed habitats. 

That idea reflects Sean Munger’s analysis for Liberation Times of an obscure term - at least for civilians- ‘signature management’.

Munger was examining a 2021 U.S. intelligence assessment that said a small amount of data appeared to show UAP demonstrating acceleration or some degree of signature management

Munger considered whether changes in altitude, low visibility or reported radar interference might reflect attempts to avoid observation. 

Puthoff takes the question further: whether a population living secretly on Earth could shape both what people detect and the conclusions they draw from it.

Drawing on Jacques Vallée’s Messengers of Deception, he suggests that such a group might deliberately encourage people to interpret UAP encounters as visits from space. In that scenario, even a genuine sighting could reinforce a misleading explanation, drawing attention away from a source here on Earth. 

His most provocative suggestion concerns the reports of reproductive encounters and hybridisation. If those accounts had any basis, Puthoff speculates, they might reflect a search for genetic diversity by 'a relatively inbred, local, isolated society on the wane and suffering from a potentially debilitating genetic syndrome'.

That brings into question the topic of hybrids, part human (or even mostly human) and part non-human.

Speaking to Liberation Times earlier this year, Lue Elizondo speculated on the notion that humans could be hybrids, adding:

“If that’s the case, if that’s true, then how much control of our own destiny do we really have?” he asked. “And are we predestined to be, you know, someone else’s pet monkey?”

Retired CIA officer John Ramirez has claimed that the agency sought to trace what he calls ‘alien DNA’ in certain families in the northeastern United States, with particular interest in their children. 

He said he learned of the alleged effort at an unclassified, one-day symposium in Virginia in 2001, where the late Gerald K. Haines, then the CIA’s chief historian, spoke about the agency’s UAP history.

Ramirez said an officer from the CIA’s Office of the Chief Scientist invited him to the symposium. CIA-sponsored postdoctoral researchers attended, and John R. Phillips, then the agency’s chief scientist, introduced Haines. Phillips’ background included over three decades at Los Alamos National Laboratory before joining the CIA in 1999.

While at Los Alamos National Laboratory, Phillips helped launch a nuclear materials security program in Russia in 1994 and joined a 1998 delegation to Kazakhstan that laid the groundwork for securing nuclear materials at the former Soviet test site at Semipalatinsk.

A source previously told Liberation Times that the CIA’s chief scientist serves as an operational gatekeeper for programs within the agency’s Directorate of Science and Technology that recover and reverse-engineer vehicles said to be of non-human origin.

Liberation Times understands that U.S. intelligence and special operations personnel have been referred to Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory after encounters they believed involved non-human beings. One source pointed to Z Division, the laboratory’s intelligence unit.

Established in 1965 under an agreement between the CIA and the Atomic Energy Commission, Z Division initially assessed foreign nuclear weapons programs. 

Its remit later expanded to chemical and biological weapons proliferation, and today’s Z Program includes a Biological Science and Security team. The wider laboratory also has the capability to perform human whole-genome sequencing and identify genetic variants.

The name ‘Z-Division’  appears in a more unusual account in Jacques Vallée’s Forbidden Science, Volume 6. In his journal entry for 28 May 2014, Vallée wrote that retired CIA officer Jim Semivan had turned to people within the Agency for answers after a disturbing encounter with unknown bibendum entities, which had occurred decades earlier.

According to the unnamed sources Vallée cited, officers Semivan trusted told him: ‘We know what it is, you’ll get a visit from Z-Division.’ Vallée wrote that Semivan was offered an additional clearance that would allow the unit to brief him, but declined. 

Liberation Times has contacted Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory for comment regarding the allegations.

In light of Puthoff’s paper, sources have told Liberation Times that no single explanation may account for the reported phenomenon. 

They suggest it could involve extraterrestrials, isolated human populations, extraterrestrials stranded on or colonising Earth, and interdimensional beings, as suggested by Puthoff. 

The sources also claim that motives may vary within each group, with attitudes toward humanity ranging from benevolent to indifferent or hostile. In their accounts, many of these beings are personally flawed like humans.

Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, who directed a U.S. UAP investigative effort known as AATIP, told Congress in November 2024 that reports near military and nuclear facilities raised the possibility of surveillance or reconnaissance.

Elizondo, speaking to Liberation Times earlier this year, also warned against assuming that even classified analysts can know the motives of a non-human intelligence.

“There may be people in the US government who think they know the intent.

“But the reality is there’s no way to confirm it.”

In that same interview, Elizondo asked whether it is possible that humans and non-human intelligence “share a common ancestry”.

He added that alien life may have “really evolved right here”.

In May 2025, one of Hal Puthoff’s associates, Dr Eric W. Davis, a theoretical physicist, former Pentagon contractor, and propulsion researcher, told lawmakers during a multi-panel event that crews of some UAP, according to his own sources, include Nordic, Reptilian, Grey and Insectoid beings.  

Liberation Times has previously been told by an intelligence community source about alleged reptile-like beings referred to as “strangers”.

The source described them as aggressive beings based beneath the Moon’s surface and claimed they were competing with a ‘Nordic’ group characterised as more empathetic.

The source did not describe a conventional war:

“Competition between the sides may be nearly as old as humanity itself. What I've heard described isn't an outright war, but rather a scaled-down adversarial relationship.

“It's unclear which sides have aligned with international governments, or which sides are cooperating with factions within the program. It's quite possible that every government has had to manage this competition among the sides.”

Speaking about the Moon in a previous interview with Liberation Times, Lue Elizondo stated:

“There are classified sources of information that I am unable to elaborate,” he said, “that indicate that the Moon is or was perhaps of particular interest by something or someone else other than us.”

David Grusch, a former U.S. Air Force intelligence officer and UAP whistleblower, has cultivated a network of sources with ties to alleged secret government programs involving UAP.

Speaking to Joe Rogan recently, Grusch described a purported crash involving a craft he associated with reptilian beings. He said dead grey beings were also reported at the site and suggested the crash might have followed a clash between the two groups

In the same interview, Grusch said he had watched contemporary footage filmed during a crash retrieval. It showed several dead, human-looking figures with pale, bluish-white skin, he claimed. 

He described them as “very, very beautiful” and compared them to Greek gods. Grusch linked that comparison to a remark he said retired Major General Neil McCasland, a former commander of the Air Force Research Laboratory, had made to Blink-182 singer Tom DeLonge.

McCasland went missing in February 2026.

In their 2017 book Sekret Machines: Gods, DeLonge and co-author Peter Levenda wrote that a senior military figure had urged DeLonge to take a closer look at Greek mythology after reviewing some of the material they had gathered.

The comparison also echoes a possibility explored in Hal Puthoff’s paper: that extraterrestrials who arrived on Earth long ago and remained here may have entered ancient accounts of gods.

For many ancient Greeks, the gods were an active presence in everyday life. People poured out wine as an offering at home, while Athenians honoured Athena as the protector of their city. As historian Tom Holland put it, “without understanding what the gods meant to the Athenians or to the Romans, you can’t understand them.”

Liberation Times understands that these alleged beings vary in appearance, including in skin tone, hair colour and height.

Grusch also spoke to Rogan about different subtypes of species, including grey beings.

Sources describe hostilities between some of these alleged non-human groups. The U.S. government is also alleged to have played a role in shooting down some of the vehicles attributed to them.

The broader history of how these groups, their factions and human governments may have dealt with one another remains unclear.

One source told Liberation Times that intelligence analysts read into the matter have reached a stark assessment: This is not our planet. It is their planet.

item.title: Behind the White House’s UFO Silence: Alleged Briefings, Investigations and an Uncertain Path to Disclosure
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: Throughout the summer, rumours swirled that President Donald Trump was preparing an extraordinary announcement. He would tell Americans, and the world, that we are not alone in the universe.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 17 November 2026

Throughout the summer, rumours swirled that President Donald Trump was preparing an extraordinary announcement.

He would tell Americans, and the world, that we are not alone in the universe.

Several sources urged Liberation Times to take the prospect seriously. Sources familiar with the President’s inner circle and members of his family expressed alarm and confidence that he could deliver disclosure.

That announcement has yet to come.

Liberation Times is aware of contact between White House staff and advocates for transparency on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP). Some discussions stretched late into the night, discussing navigation of alleged UAP programs involving non-human lifeforms.

Alongside those conversations, a formal advisory structure took shape.

In June, an official from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) described the arrangements to Liberation Times. The official said ODNI had established a UAP Governance Board alongside the FBI and Department of War (DoW).

Its charter includes coordinating investigations, improving data collection and supporting declassification.

Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb publicly announced one of its supporting groups. In a 13 June article, he described assembling the UAP Science Advisory Council. Loeb said government agencies had tasked him with bringing together scientists to help investigate the phenomenon.

Other organisations also joined discussions at ODNI. They included the Disclosure Foundation, a nonprofit advocating UAP transparency, and To The Stars, a media company involved in UAP research. The Sol Foundation, a think tank established to advance wider understanding of UAP, was also understood to be present.*

Aaron Lukas, the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, publicly identified their involvement on 17 September. He thanked both organisations and Loeb’s council for participating as advisers to the Governance Board.

However, other advisory councils working alongside ODNI, the FBI and DoW remain undisclosed.

Questions about ODNI’s role also extend to an alleged operation to attract UAP. As Liberation Times previously reported, released government records describe a senior intelligence official witnessing glowing orbs at a sensitive U.S. testing facility.

Jordan Flowers, executive director of the Disclosure Foundation, an advocacy group campaigning for UAP transparency, has alleged that these encounters formed part of a successful ODNI luring operation, although the released records do not explicitly confirm that purpose.

Separately, journalist Ross Coulthart has alleged that Trump authorised military operations that resulted in UAP being shot down. The White House left Liberation Times’ questions about both the alleged luring operation and shootdown authorisations unanswered.

On CBS’s 60 Minutes, Trump denied hearing about a secret UAP program hidden from presidents. 

He promised to investigate immediately following the interview.

Liberation Times subsequently asked whether he had followed through. A White House spokesperson replied:

‘Refer you to the President’s comments.’

The response left unanswered whether Trump had indeed investigated.

In the interview, when pushed on whether he was interested in the topic because other people were, Trump said:

“I would like to find out whether or not it's true. I will tell you, you have a lot of very solid people that believe it's true.”

The interview came amid extensive discussion of the allegations involving such programs by people in his orbit.

Fox News host Sean Hannity, a longtime Trump ally, interviewed former U.S. Air Force intelligence specialist Dylan Borland - a UAP whistleblower - and former FBI agent Ben Hansen. Their conversation covered alleged recovered craft and government secrecy. Hannity said he would raise the issue with the President when he next saw him.

Television psychologist Phil McGraw, better known as Dr Phil, interviewed former Air Force intelligence officer and UAP whistleblower David Grusch. They discussed Grusch’s allegations of secret retrieval efforts involving non-human craft and their occupants.

There are also accounts of information reaching Trump during his first term.

Former Pentagon official Luis Elizondo described one such route in his 2024 memoir, Imminent. He wrote that Jay Stratton, who led the government’s UAP Task Force, briefed National Security Council members. According to Elizondo, those officials subsequently briefed Trump.

The President’s son, Donald Trump Jr., has also interviewed Elizondo three times on his Triggered podcast. Their discussions have covered UAP and alleged secret government programs.

Republican Congressman Eric Burlison also recounted an alleged briefing given directly to Trump, attributing the account to David Grusch, who previously served as a special adviser on Burlison’s staff.

He said, according to what he was told, Trump had been briefed on alleged human-alien hybrids during his first term, adding that the briefing took place while Trump was facing impeachment proceedings.

“He had like this existential briefing that just kind of rocked his worldview,” Burlison said.

Burlison added that he had been told Trump joked that then-Congressman Adam Schiff ‘must be one of them’, referring to the alleged hybrid beings.

Liberation Times also understands that Trump’s new Chief of Staff is very aware of alleged UAP programs. 

The White House named Stephen Miller Chief of Staff on 6 November, following Republican losses in the midterm elections.

Miller previously served as Trump’s deputy chief of staff.

In August, Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated that Miller was overseeing the UAP portfolio. Sources told Liberation Times that his work included investigating alleged hidden programs to retrieve and reverse-engineer non-human craft.

Congress member and UAP transparency advocate, Tim Burchett recently told Cabot Phillips that Stephen Miller had told him:

"There's some people that are in government that I feel like are very bad people that don't want us to have this information for whatever reason.”

Miller’s promotion has left uncertainty over who now leads that work.

Republican Congressman Eric Burlison, a member of the congressional UAP Caucus, voiced similar concerns during a 10 November interview. Speaking to journalist Matt Laslo for Ask a Pol UAP, he said Trump had taken Miller off the UAP topic.

Burlison questioned whether Miller would retain time for it. He also said he did not know whether anyone would replace him. 

The uncertainty comes as Congress considers another route to disclosure.

On 22 July, the House adopted Burlison’s UAP Disclosure Act as an amendment to the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. The proposal would establish an independent records review board and extend disclosure requirements to covered government contractors.

Its fate in the final defence bill remains unresolved.

Meanwhile, the administration has continued releasing records through its Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, or PURSUE. The Department of War announced the initiative’s first release on 8 May.

The releases have not clarified what the White House has learned about the origins of UAP or the intentions of any entities behind them, nor how much the administration intends to disclose.

Democrats will take control of both chambers of Congress in January 2027, when the 120th Congress begins. Their commitment to UAP transparency will face a test after Republican-led hearings and investigations championed by Representatives Anna Paulina Luna, Tim Burchett and Eric Burlison, including through Luna’s declassification task force. 

Speaking about the current situation within Washington D.C., Jordan Flowers, executive director of the Disclosure Foundation, told Liberation Times:

“The next several weeks are a test of whether Congress can lock in real progress before leadership changes on January 3, through another hearing and the full UAP Disclosure Act in the NDAA, and whether the new majority will build on that work with a select committee that has subpoena power.

“At the White House, the public messaging has been inconsistent, but the PURSUE releases show continued interest, and our job is to keep this a bipartisan issue anchored in national security and accountability for waste, fraud, and abuse.”

Democratic Representative André Carson, who chaired the first public congressional UAP hearing in more than 50 years in May 2022, is reportedly pushing for a dedicated UAP select committee.

Carson, whose seat on the House Intelligence Committee gives him a direct role in overseeing U.S. intelligence agencies and their classified activities, previously discussed the idea with journalist Matt Laslo in 2025. 

Commenting on that possibility, Flowers told Liberation Times:

“In the 120th Congress, a select committee on UAP led by Representative André Carson would be wonderful progress: it would not face the six-month renewal question that has hung over the current task force, and it would have subpoena power from day one.

“Representative Carson’s experience on both Intelligence and Oversight would also make him well placed to connect the two committees that matter most on this topic, and we hope any new structure stays bipartisan and builds on the work Republican members have already done.”

Any potential disclosure could expose intelligence capabilities that extend well beyond UAP.

Sources previously told Liberation Times that the CIA’s Weapons and Counterproliferation Mission Center (WCPMC) has helped assess the phenomenon’s potential non-human origins. They described work to identify the different intelligences that might control these objects and assess their intentions.

According to those sources, WCPMC drew on intelligence collected across the U.S. government. This included space-based collection by the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), which develops and operates reconnaissance satellites.

They also identified the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA), National Security Agency (NSA) and National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) as contributors.

The sources described inputs spanning signals intelligence, measurement and signature intelligence, and geospatial intelligence. They said WCPMC collected and analysed UAP information from the atmosphere, space and undersea environments.

The CIA publicly confirms WCPMC’s existence. It describes its mission centres as combining operational, analytical and technical capabilities to address national security threats. 

An intelligence-community source told Liberation Times that detailed technical assessments of UAP from the WCPMC were shared among specialists across intelligence agencies. Finished assessments were then prepared for senior policymakers.

Such intelligence work, alongside the recovery and reverse-engineering of foreign technology, serves U.S. national security.

Some of the capabilities involved may remain classified even if the administration chooses to acknowledge any possible non-human presence.

One potential route to disclosure is the separate UAP effort allegedly operating under White House oversight.

If reports of luring and shootdown operations are accurate, that effort could give the administration evidence obtained independently of existing programs.

It might provide a path to disclosure while protecting sensitive intelligence sources and methods.

Whether that effort has produced such evidence, and whether Trump intends to release it, remains unclear.

*Updated on 26 November 2026

item.title: Trump Pushed UAP Disclosure Further Than Any President - Now He Should Press Congress to Make It Law
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: There are rare moments when a nation decides, in the span of a few weeks, whether a truth kept from its people for generations finally sees the light of day.
item.content:encoded:
Opinion

Written by Kevin Wright - 6 November 2026

Executive orders fade. Only the UAP Disclosure Act, kept in the final defense bill before the window closes in December, can make disclosure permanent.

There are rare moments when a nation decides, in the span of a few weeks, whether a truth kept from its people for generations finally sees the light of day.

We are witnessing one of those moments. The door is open. It will not stay open for long, and history will remember who chose to walk through it and who let it swing shut.

For the first time in eighty years, a sitting president ordered the government to stop hiding what it knows about unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP).

Through the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE), the Trump administration has released more than 155,000 pages of records to the public across seven tranches, along with videos, photographs, and audio files.

Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller has driven the effort from inside the White House. Harvard’s Avi Loeb has lent it scientific seriousness.

After decades of ridicule, we are finally talking about records, not rumors. That is real, and the president deserves credit for it.

But credit is not the same as completion, and the work is now in danger of stopping well short of the finish line.

The releases, as striking as they are to many, have not settled any questions, and even those closest to the issue say so.

Ryan Graves, the former Navy pilot whose sworn testimony helped drag this subject into the daylight in July 2023, now sits on the very UAP Science Advisory Council the administration formed under Harvard’s Loeb to help resolve the mystery.

And even Graves has called what has been released so far unsatisfactory: short infrared clips rather than the high-grade sensor data that would allow proper scientific analysis of these encounters.

When one of the administration’s own advisors says the disclosure effort falls short, the problem is not the president’s intent or a missing directive from him. It is a missing law with the power to enforce it.

The president has called for openness. The departments and agencies that hold the files have answered with something short of it: a release of what they choose, at the pace they choose, while keeping back what they would rather not surrender.

That is not disclosure. It is the shadow of it. And a shadow is precisely what the people who have guarded these secrets for decades are counting on.

In July, the House did its part. It adopted Representative Eric Burlison’s (R-MO) UAP Disclosure Act as an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2027.

The bill is modeled on the President John F. Kennedy Assassination Records Collection Act of 1992, which did not simply release a handful of documents.

It built a system. It created a permanent collection of the assassination records at the National Archives, established an independent review board empowered to hunt down documents and force agencies to justify every secret they wished to keep, set a legal presumption that the records would be made public, and fixed a deadline for opening them.

Burlison’s bill applies that same architecture to the UAP question, extending the duty of disclosure even to the private contractors who have sheltered behind government secrecy for years.

That bill now sits in conference, where the House and Senate will reconcile their versions and write the final text, likely by mid-December.

Here is what should alarm anyone who cares about this issue. For three years running, UAP transparency language was quietly stymied, stripped, or killed.

In 2023, the last time the UAPDA went to conference, it was gutted in the same room, by the same committees (and many of the same members) who hold the disclosure legislation in their hands.

The same fate waits again unless the president and his team make it unmistakably clear, in public and in private, that Burlison’s language stays in the final bill.

Some in the administration will resist. They will argue that the president already controls disclosure, so why hand authority to an independent board and tie his own hands.

It is a fair question, and it deserves an honest answer.

The answer is that the president’s control is largely an illusion. He has signed the directives. He has ordered the releases. And still the pace crawls, the best material stays buried, and the questions that matter most go unanswered.

Why?

Because the so-called Legacy Program, the alleged apparatus of crash retrieval and reverse engineering that former intelligence officer David Grusch described under oath to Congress, is reportedly run out of the very departments and agencies the president commands.

Asking those offices to surrender their own deepest secrets is asking the fox to guard the henhouse. An executive order without an enforcement mechanism is a wish written on White House letterhead. The people slow-walking the president are not his partners in this effort. They are the obstacle to it.

So, understand what this UAPDA amendment to the NDAA actually proposes to do.

It does not take the files out of the president’s hands. It takes them out of the hands of the people inside his own administration who are defying him.

The independent review board is not the president’s rival. It is the hammer his directives have never had, a body armed with subpoena power and a statutory clock that can finally force the holdouts to produce. Something will have to compel them, kicking and screaming.

For anyone worried about the president surrendering his authority, read the bill.

He nominates all nine civilian members of the review board; then the Senate confirms them, so the body that oversees disclosure is staffed by his choices, not imposed on him.

The bill also preserves the executive’s authority to postpone the release of genuinely sensitive material on national security grounds. The president keeps the brake, but gains the engine.

There is more.

A law carries a credibility that no executive action can.

Right now, disclosure is coordinated by a UAP Governance Board, an interagency body that the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) established with the FBI and the Department of War.

But a coordinating board can only release what the agencies beneath it are willing to surface, and if the allegations hold, the most sensitive records are buried so deep, inside compartmented programs and the files of private contractors, that they may lie beyond the reach of the board itself.

Even the scientists the administration recruited under Loeb have been held to material already released, and when Loeb’s council asked the agencies for more, the custodians refused, citing national security.

A release administered by the departments and agencies, some of the alleged gatekeepers, from beginning to end, will always invite the same question: what did they choose not to show us?

A disclosure compelled by an independent board, under the law, retires that question for good. The president does not weaken his hand by accepting outside verification. He is the only one who can give this effort the legitimacy that silences the skeptics.

Then there is the matter of legacy, and here the choice could not be starker.

Executive power is borrowed, and it is temporary.

Everything this administration has built through its own authority can be undone by the next one, quietly, with a single signature, on the first afternoon of a new term in January 2029.

Only a statute endures. The Kennedy records law outlived the president who signed it precisely because it was law and not preference.

If President Trump wants disclosure to stand as his legacy rather than a footnote the next administration erases, there is exactly one way to secure it: carve it into the permanent law of the United States.

And let no one pretend that doing nothing keeps the president in control.

On January 3, the gavels change hands. A new majority in the U.S. House and Senate will control the committees, the subpoenas, and the investigations.

If this issue is left open, the president loses command of it. He hands the files, the framing, and the credit to his opposition.

The real choice is not whether to keep control or give it up. It is whether to lock disclosure in now, on cooperative terms, with his name on it, or to watch it pass to the Party that just defeated him. Inaction does not protect his control; rather, it forfeits it.

Consider, too, what the country just said out loud.

Only days ago, Americans across the political spectrum sent an unmistakable message that they are finished with a government that hides the truth and shields its own. The right to know is not a partisan slogan. It is the oldest promise a free people makes to itself, the promise that those who govern will answer to those they govern.

A president who meets that demand by joining hands with Congress to make transparency permanent is not on the defensive.

No, he is out in front, leading the parade that the public is already marching in.

The administration also ignores a hard political calculation at its peril. Until now, this fight has been genuinely bipartisan, which is the only reason it has gotten this far. The moment the new majority takes the gavels, the temptation will be enormous to turn transparency into a cudgel; to convert an honest search for the truth into one more investigation aimed squarely at this president and the agencies beneath him.

The White House is going to face a wall of those battles in the next two years. Settling UAP disclosure now, through a neutral process written into law while it can still be done on friendly terms, takes that weapon off the table before it can be picked up. It converts an open-ended partisan probe into an orderly process governed by rules that both parties already support. One less front to defend and one lasting victory to claim.

This is not a fringe demand. In a CBS News/YouGov poll this summer, 84 percent of Americans, across both parties, said the government knows more about UFOs than it is telling. Democrats, Republicans, and independents agree on little right now. They agree on this.

This is a direct appeal to the president, to Stephen Miller, and to every member of Congress who has carried this fight on their shoulders.

Do not let the conference committee do in the dark what it did in 2023.

The men and women who hold the pen in that room have names, and they should hear from the White House this week.

Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) and Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-LA) in the House. Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) in the Senate.

House Armed Services Chairman Mike Rogers (R-AL) and Senate Armed Services Chairman Roger Wicker (R-MS), who steer the defense bill.

House Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford (R-AR) and Senate Intelligence Chairman Tom Cotton (R-AR), who guard the classification lines.

Tell them plainly that Representative Burlison’s UAP Disclosure Act stays in the final NDAA. Not a hollowed-out version. Not another commission to study the question for another year. Not another shelf at the National Archives. The real thing, with the review board, subpoena power, and the teeth intact.

We have waited eighty years.

Generations of pilots, scientists, and ordinary witnesses were told to stay quiet, that it was nothing, that they had not seen what they plainly saw, and allegedly threatened, harassed, intimidated, and worse.

Remember: for the first time in this republic’s history, a president chose to pull back the curtain on this enigma. The only question left is whether he finishes the job while the power to finish it is still his, or whether he lets it pass to the people who just defeated him and watches them take the credit. Or worse, the buck gets passed to another generation to fight for what is theirs, the right to know.

A handful of officials and professional staff will write the final conference report in a non-public room over the next few weeks, carrying out their respective Chairman’s and Ranking Member’s directives.

This is where the final decision on the UAPDA will be made.

Trump does not need to sign anything new or issue another order.

Trump needs only to make his will plain to those with waning influence and power in Congress, including the leaders of both chambers: the UAP Disclosure Act stays in the NDAA, intact.

That leverage is very real, but it expires the moment the gavels change hands in January.

He should use it now and make the people’s right to know the law of the land.

item.title: Trump Still Holds the Cards on UFO Disclosure After Midterm Defeat
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: Attempts to persuade President Donald Trump to deliver a disclosure speech on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) before the midterm elections have failed.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 4 November 2026

Attempts to persuade President Donald Trump to deliver a disclosure speech on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) before the midterm elections have failed.

Democrats have now won control of both the House and Senate.

Republicans, however, retain their majorities until the outgoing Congress’s term ends on 3 January 2027, while Trump’s presidential term is due to end on 20 January 2029.

For now, Republicans still control the congressional agenda, and Trump continues to lead the executive branch that holds much of the information disclosure advocates want released.

The House adopted Representative Eric Burlison’s UAP Disclosure Act (UAPDA) amendment on 22 July 2026, as part of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2027.

Those provisions now need to survive negotiations over a final bill that both chambers can pass and send to President Trump.

Republican congressional leaders will have substantial influence over whether they are retained.

If fully passed, despite successive failed attempts, the UAPDA would strengthen the records system established under the FY2024 NDAA.

In its House-passed form, it would:

  • Require agencies to preserve and transfer UAP records to the National Archives, including covered records under government control through contracts or other agreements

  • Establish an independent, nine-member review board, appointed by the President with Senate confirmation, to examine records, hear testimony and use subpoena powers

  • Require full disclosure within 25 years of a record’s creation, unless the President certifies that the harm from release would outweigh the public interest under the legislation’s criteria

  • Require a Controlled Disclosure Campaign Plan, with continuing reviews of information whose release is postponed

  • Require the government to acquire privately held recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence through eminent domain, should such material exist, and make it available to the review board.

The President would still have authority to postpone certain executive branch releases under the legislation.

The review board would operate until 30 September 2030, with the wider disclosure obligations continuing until the Archivist certifies that all covered records have been made public in accordance with the law.

Its purpose is to carry disclosure beyond a single presidency, making it harder for a change of administration or congressional control to bring the process to a halt.

For now, President Trump can authorise further UAP releases and explain what his administration knows about whistleblower claims that the U.S. government and its contractors have recovered non-human vehicles and are working to reverse-engineer them.

Liberation Times understands that several insiders within Trump’s personal circle remain convinced he will disclose. Some have even expressed concern that he could reveal too much.

Sean Hannity, Dr Phil and Matt Gaetz are among the media figures in Trump’s circle who have repeatedly discussed UAP and interviewed whistleblowers and witnesses.

New York Post columnist Cindy Adams, a longstanding friend of the President, last week urged the U.S. government to release evidence of non-human intelligence for independent scientific scrutiny.

The President’s daughter-in-law, Lara Trump, has also suggested he may already have a speech prepared on extraterrestrial life. Speaking on the Pod Force One podcast earlier this year, she said:

“I’ve heard kind of around, I think my father-in-law has actually said it, that there is some speech that he has, that I guess at the right time, I don’t know when the right time is, he’s going to break out and talk about and it has to do with maybe some sort of extraterrestrial life.”

However, others who have spoken to Liberation Times doubt that the President has the character or sustained commitment to deliver meaningful disclosure. And following midterm losses, the President appears to be increasingly unhinged, according to reports.

The administration has continued publishing files through PURSUE, the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters.

The Pentagon-led initiative followed Trump’s direction to identify and release government files relating to UAP and extraterrestrial life.

Among the released tranches are accounts from special agents who described a silent triangular object hovering before accelerating rapidly, and a senior intelligence official at ODNI who reported encounters with glowing orbs.

Sources speaking to Liberation Times say investigative work within the White House has also been examining allegations of concealed crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering programs, led by Trump Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy, Stephen Miller.

Little has been said publicly about that work, or what the administration has learned from the encounters described in the PURSUE files.

For years, the House and Senate intelligence committees backed UAP legislation, while public hearings brought the subject to a wider audience.

As those committees and some of their leading supporters became less vocal, other House lawmakers carried the public push for disclosure forward.

With UAP now a White House priority, that effort has reached the highest level of the U.S. government.

With control of both chambers from January 2027, Democrats will have an opportunity to press the White House for more information.

That could include scrutiny of allegations that Trump authorised UAP shootdowns and that U.S. officials conducted operations to attract the objects.

The White House and Pentagon have not commented to Liberation Times on the alleged shootdowns or operations to lure UAP, despite repeated requests.

Representative Eric Burlison has already spoken publicly about a classified briefing concerning an apparent attempt to attract UAP.

In an interview with Dr Phil published on 15 October 2026, Burlison recalled that, in the autumn of 2025, ODNI officials had been winding down an investigation that had lasted years and produced few answers.

He was later called back to the same office. Burlison recalled being told:

“Sir, things have changed. We really need to bring you in and update you.”

According to Burlison, the new briefing concerned an encounter in late autumn 2025 at a military installation in the western United States, where personnel from several intelligence agencies had witnessed unusual objects.

Speaking separately to Annie Frey, Burlison described an effort to create conditions that would attract UAP so they could be documented. He said:

“That briefing is the one everybody wants.

“Yes, other members of Congress have heard about this. Leader Scalise got the briefing along with a couple of other members.

“I had only told Leader Scalise about this, and now everybody wants this briefing.”

If Democrats receive the same briefing, they could press the administration to explain what happened, who authorised the alleged operations and what evidence was obtained.

They could also demand that more of those findings be made public.

Before the election, the New York Post reported on 31 October that Democrats were preparing to make UAP transparency a focus if they regained the House.

Representative André Carson, who chaired the 2022 public House intelligence hearing on UAP, accused the administration of moving too slowly on disclosure.

Citing unnamed insiders, the newspaper also reported plans for a Democratic UFO caucus and a select committee to supplant the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, led by Republican Representative Anna Paulina Luna.

If Democrats follow through, they could put Trump under pressure to explain his administration’s activities while competing to deliver the transparency he has promised.

For a President who has sought credit for opening the government’s UAP files, being overtaken by the opposition would present a political problem.

However, the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, which oversees Luna’s task force, appears set to prioritise investigations into Trump and his administration.

Representative Robert Garcia, the committee’s top Democrat and expected next chairman, posted a two-word warning on Tuesday night:

“Lawyer up.”

Garcia has already outlined four main areas for investigation: allegations of Trump family corruption, abuses by Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Department of Homeland Security, corporate corruption, and the Jeffrey Epstein scandal.

Republicans still have the closing weeks of this Congress to secure the disclosure legislation. And Trump has more than two years left in office to decide how far he is willing to go.

He still has time to deliver the moment his friend Dr Phil has described: the government standing at a podium and declaring, “We are not alone.”

If such a moment were to occur, it would certainly change the entire political landscape, both at home and abroad.

item.title: FBI Declines To Explain Deployment Of Agents Who Encountered Triangular UFO
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: The FBI has declined to explain why agents equipped with optical and thermal surveillance equipment were deployed to observation posts at a sensitive national security site in the western United States, where they reported encountering a silent black triangular object.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 31 October 2026

The FBI has declined to explain why agents equipped with optical and thermal surveillance equipment were deployed to observation posts at a sensitive national security site in the western United States, where they reported encountering a silent black triangular object.

According to a Pentagon memorandum documenting the agents’ account of the encounter, the object rose vertically above a ridgeline, hovered for approximately twenty seconds, then accelerated rapidly before banking and descending into a canyon.

But the purpose of that surveillance assignment remains unclear.

The Bureau’s involvement in Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) investigations appears to extend beyond this encounter.

In reporting published on 3 September, journalist Matt Laslo documented Representative Anna Paulina Luna discussing an FBI unit called the Special Investigations Group, or SIG, and showing a commemorative UAP coin.

Luna told Laslo:

“We work directly with them for our investigation”

Luna’s comments follow earlier public acknowledgment of FBI investigations into UAP.

On 3 February 2025, The Debrief reported that an FBI spokesperson had confirmed:

“the FBI investigates Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena when there is potential for a violation of federal law”

The spokesperson also described the Bureau’s role in gathering and analysing intelligence to address security threats.

Former Navy pilot Ryan Graves told the publication that Americans for Safe Aerospace had spent approximately eighteen months working with an FBI team known as the UAP Working Group, assisting investigations involving reports from pilots and veterans.

The FBI operates within the Department of Justice, outside the leadership structures of the Department of War and CIA.

Under 28 U.S.C. § 535, it can investigate suspected federal crimes involving personnel from those organisations, providing a potential avenue for scrutiny of alleged UAP-related wrongdoing.

The released records do not establish whether SIG was involved in this encounter or whether the agents’ deployment concerned suspected criminal activity.

The Triangle Case

Two records released by the Department of War on 23 October, as part of its seventh tranche of UAP files, describe the encounter: an FBI statement and a witness debrief prepared by the Pentagon’s All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO).

The incident took place in 2026. The precise date, location and identities of those involved are redacted.

AARO describes the agents’ assignment as ‘routine observation support.’

Liberation Times asked the FBI why Special Agents were deployed with optical and thermal surveillance equipment, whether they were conducting a specific operation, and whether their presence was connected to previous reports of unidentified aerial objects.

Liberation Times also asked whether the Bureau had identified the object, whether the incident remained under investigation, and whether photographic, video or thermal evidence had been obtained.

The FBI National Press Office responded:

“We have nothing additional to add to the documents.”

The released records do not establish whether the witnesses were FBI agents. Liberation Times has subsequently emailed the Bureau to ask whether the agents worked for it.*

AARO’s memorandum describes two witnesses at a primary observation post with optical equipment and a tripod-mounted sensor system initially facing east.

At a separate post, a third witness was scanning west with long-range thermal equipment.

That witness detected an object and alerted the others by radio.

The two agents moved across the hilltop to obtain a view to the west. The terrain prevented them from quickly repositioning the main tripod-mounted thermal system, so one advanced with binoculars and a handheld thermal monocular.

The FBI statement identifies the initial alert as coming from Observation Post 6.

The deployment suggests a coordinated surveillance assignment: personnel at separate observation posts were using optical and thermal equipment and communicating by radio, enabling them to respond when an aerial object was detected.

AARO also records that the two principal witnesses had extensive operational experience working alongside government agencies and academic studies involving unmanned aerial systems. They regularly observed conventional aircraft around the site.

What brought that experience and equipment together at this location is something the FBI has chosen not to explain beyond the released records.

In the statement reproduced in the FBI file, the agents described ‘a substantial, nonreflective, dark black triangular object most resembling a delta wing drone.’

They estimated its wingspan at nine to fifteen feet, its length at six to nine feet, and its thickness at one to two feet. AARO gave a wingspan estimate of thirteen to fifteen feet.

The thermal observation was unusual.

One agent wrote:

‘I viewed the object through a handheld thermal device and noted it appeared hotter than ambient temperature with a completely consistent thermal signature across the entire airframe and no visible exhaust gases.’

AARO’s account describes a featureless surface, without visible windows, rotating elements, intakes or control surfaces.

According to that account, the object climbed vertically for around ten seconds, reaching an estimated 200 to 300 feet above the ridgeline while maintaining a level orientation.

It then stopped climbing and hovered for approximately twenty seconds, with no apparent drift or oscillation.

The memorandum states:

‘The transition from stable hover to high-speed horizontal flight occurred without observable acceleration ramp, gradual pitching or momentum.’

The witnesses compared its departure speed to that of a military fighter jet.

AARO adds an important qualification:

‘No instrumented speed measurement was obtained.’

The object reportedly banked and descended along the canyon terrain, disappearing from view within approximately two to three seconds.

The handheld thermal device lost contact as the object moved beyond its narrow field of view. Visual tracking continued until the terrain obscured it.

The agents reported hearing no sound.

A ground survey the following morning found no wreckage, ground scarring or vegetation damage in the canyon drainage.

The reported behaviour overlaps with two of the ‘five observables’ popularised by former Pentagon UAP official Luis Elizondo.

  • Lift without apparent propulsion - reported: The memorandum describes vertical ascent and stable hovering without visible rotors, exhaust or another identifiable propulsion system.

  • Sudden acceleration - reported: AARO describes a transition from hovering to rapid horizontal flight without an observable acceleration ramp.

  • Hypersonic velocity without expected signatures - not established: The witnesses compared its speed to a fighter jet, but no instrumented speed measurement was obtained.

  • Low observability - not established: The matte-black appearance and lack of distinct propulsion hot spots do not demonstrate cloaking or radar evasion. The object was observed visually and through thermal equipment.

  • Trans-medium travel - not reported: Neither record describes the object crossing between air and water or travelling through another medium.

The FBI document also includes nine images depicting the same landscape, with a triangular shape appearing in successive positions.

They appear to illustrate the reported sequence, but the file does not identify them as photographs captured during the encounter.

The Department of War’s online description of the AARO memorandum states:

‘AARO considers this incident to warrant further investigation due to the close alignment of the phenomena’s reported morphological features and kinematic profiles with those of other reported incidents in the western United States region.’

The description does not identify which other incidents AARO was referring to.

Is The U.S. Government Luring UAP?

The FBI’s response comes amid allegations that U.S. officials deliberately tried to attract UAP during a separate series of encounters in late 2025.

That earlier case involved glowing orbs at a military installation and was documented in previous government releases.

Both cases were reported in the western United States, but the released records do not establish whether they occurred at the same facility.

Representative Eric Burlison has since described how previous sightings prompted officials to send personnel to the site - and how certain activity on the range appeared to attract further UAP.

Speaking to Dr. Phil in an interview released on 15 October, the Missouri congressman described a marked change in the briefings he received from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI).

In the autumn of 2025, he said, officials had been concluding an investigation which had lasted years and produced few answers.

He was then called back to the same office for a different briefing.

Burlison recalled being told:

“Sir, things have changed. We really need to bring you in and update you.”

He said the new briefing concerned an encounter late in the autumn of 2025, when personnel from ODNI, the CIA, FBI and Department of War intelligence were present at a western military installation.

According to Burlison, those personnel saw glowing orbs hovering silently, accelerating suddenly and, in some instances, splitting into two.

He said the first tranches of President Trump’s UAP releases had allowed him to discuss aspects of the incident publicly.

Burlison was discussing the same late-2025 encounter Liberation Times reported on in July, documented in an FBI interview with a senior intelligence official, a firsthand narrative and images of objects near a helicopter.

Sources have told Liberation Times that the late-2025 encounters occurred at White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico.

Disclosure Foundation executive director Jordan Flowers characterised that event as a successful UAP luring operation.

Burlison described the location as “somewhat of a hotspot”, where objects had appeared historically.

More specifically, he said: “they tend to show up whenever they do certain activity.”

According to Burlison, recent reports prompted officials to send personnel to observe. During that deployment, he said, they experienced the interactions described in the released records.

He cautioned against interpreting this as an ability to summon the objects on demand.

Instead, he compared it to a hunter knowing where deer tend to travel and using scents to attract them.

He said:

“You can kind of attract them, but it doesn't guarantee an outcome.”

Burlison also said intelligence personnel in a helicopter came within approximately ten feet of the orbs, which appeared to respond and form deliberate formations.

He told Dr. Phil:

“These orbs were responding and operating intelligently.”

The White House has also faced questions about alleged UAP luring and shootdown operations.

As Liberation Times reported in September, the White House had not answered our questions about the alleged luring operation or journalist Ross Coulthart’s separate claim that President Trump authorised UAP shootdowns around White Sands and near Ciudad Juárez, Mexico.

*Updated on 1 November 2026

item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: President Donald Trump has left the door open to a UFO disclosure announcement, responding “I’m looking” when pressed on whether he would reveal whether Earth has been visited by non-human intelligence and whether the United States is reverse-engineering its technology.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 16 October 2026

President Donald Trump has left the door open to a UFO disclosure announcement, responding “I’m looking” when asked whether he would reveal the truth about alleged alien visits to Earth and U.S. efforts to reverse-engineer non-human technology.

Speaking to Newsmax host Rob Finnerty in a White House interview on 15 October, Trump recounted conversations with military pilots who described objects they could not explain.

His remarks come after months of efforts by disclosure advocates to persuade him to make a public statement confirming that a non-human presence is interacting with humanity.

Finnerty put the issue directly to the President:

“No president has ever been willing to step to the microphone and finally disclose the truth. Are aliens real? Have we been visited? Are we reverse engineering their technology? Will you do that?”

Trump replied:

“Well, let me just tell you, it’s very interesting. I wasn’t much of a believer. I have friends that are like, that’s all they can talk about.”

He added:

“I do know we see some pretty strange things.”

Trump then described speaking to approximately five or six Air Force pilots about their encounters, emphasising that he considered them credible witnesses.

“These are solid people. These aren’t conspiracy theorists or anything else.”

According to Trump, the pilots told him they had seen things while flying that they had never encountered before. He described one account involving an object apparently outperforming an American fighter jet:

“In one case he saw a round object, which is not an ideal shape for going fast, that went faster by four times than an F-22.”

Trump said he had asked whether the object could have been a comet or something else, and that the pilot rejected that explanation.

Finnerty then returned to his original question, asking whether Trump would be the president to take the step he had described.

Trump responded:

“I’m looking.”

He continued:

“Again, I’m not high on the list of that particular subject.”

He gave no timetable for a presidential announcement and did not directly answer whether aliens had visited Earth or whether the United States was reverse-engineering their technology.

However, Trump could not rule out providing such a speech.

On 21 July, Liberation Times reported, citing multiple sources, that a presidential speech confirming that some UFOs are of non-human origin was understood to have been prepared.

In August, Liberation Times reported that advocates were seeking to persuade Trump to deliver some form of disclosure speech before the 3 November midterm elections.

That effort included public appeals from former Air Force intelligence officer David Grusch and other whistleblowers.

Businessman and Trump donor Robert Bigelow also said he had advised the President on how to address the nation about a non-human presence.

His comments come amid successive tranches of UAP files being released under PURSUE, the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters.

Overseen by the Department of War with support from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the initiative began publishing records in May 2026 following Trump’s directive to identify and release government material relating to UFOs and UAP.

The release program followed a February exchange involving former President Barack Obama.

As Liberation Times previously reported, Obama sparked international attention when, during an interview with Brian Tyler Cohen released on 14 February, he said of aliens:

“They’re real, but I haven’t seen them.”

He subsequently clarified that he had seen no evidence during his presidency that extraterrestrials had made contact with humanity.

Asked about those remarks by Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy aboard Air Force One on 19 February, Trump accused Obama of revealing classified information, without specifying what information was supposedly classified.

“He gave classified information. He’s not supposed to be doing that.”

Although Trump said he did not know whether aliens were real, he suggested he could resolve his predecessor’s supposed indiscretion through declassification:

“I may get him out of trouble by declassifying.”

Later that day, Trump announced that he would direct the Department of War and other relevant agencies to identify and release government files concerning extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs. The first tranche of records under PURSUE followed on 8 May.

item.title: Former Army Sniper Says He Was Told of Deadly Encounter With Reptilian Beings Near Area 51
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: Former U.S. Army sniper Nick Betts recounted an alleged deadly encounter with reptilian-looking beings on the Liberty Risk podcast, released on 5 December 2025. Betts said an unnamed man who claimed to have taken part in the operation told him that U.S. personnel had entered an underground installation near Area 51, killed three beings and lost one of their own men.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 15 October 2026

Former U.S. Army sniper Nick Betts recounted an alleged deadly encounter with reptilian-looking beings on the Liberty Risk podcast, released on 5 December 2025. 

Betts said an unnamed man who claimed to have taken part in the operation told him that U.S. personnel had entered an underground installation near Area 51, killed three beings and lost one of their own men.

Betts heard the story in a hotel room in Poland. He had been travelling through Eastern Europe to film a documentary about the war in Ukraine, alongside a friend who had served in a Ranger battalion, the storyteller, an older man and another companion.

According to Betts, the storyteller and the older man had served together in the same squadron and both participated in the alleged operation. The older man was asleep elsewhere when the story was told.

Betts and his friend, whom he called ‘Ranger’, were downloading footage in their shared hotel room when the storyteller arrived with four bottles of wine. Ranger brought up aliens and asked what the man knew.

The man initially refused to answer. After further prompting, he collected their phones and placed them in a microwave, which Betts described as an improvised Faraday cage intended to block electronic signals.

He then described an alleged deployment years earlier, while serving in an unnamed squadron at Fort Bragg. The installation is home to Delta Force’s squadrons and includes Pope Army Airfield, where the U.S. Air Force’s 24th and 21st Special Tactics Squadrons are based. 

Betts referred to Joint Special Operations Command, or JSOC, during his account, but did not identify the squadron or either alleged participant.

The squadron had been on quick reaction force duty. A quick reaction force, or QRF, is held ready to respond rapidly to an emergency. It describes a role rather than a particular unit; military accounts describe infantry, Rangers and Marines performing such duties.

The storyteller said he had been at a bar when the recall came. Personnel were ordered back to base, told to collect their equipment and put on an aircraft without being briefed on their destination or mission - it was added that this was highly abnormal.

A few hours later, they landed in intense heat. Two men met them outside a hangar, brought them inside and took them to a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility, or SCIF, a secure facility for handling sensitive intelligence.

There, they were allegedly told:

“Gentlemen. Welcome to Area 51.”

The mission briefing followed. Security personnel at an underground installation a few miles away had stopped conducting their regular radio checks. A QRF had already been sent to investigate, but that team had also fallen silent.

The personnel flown in from Bragg were therefore the second QRF dispatched to the installation. According to Betts, they were tasked with entering the facility and requested and received a map and a plan for getting in and out.

Before departing, they asked to check their firearms’ sights at a range. They were told they would not need those guns and were instead issued unfamiliar weapons that did not take magazines. Betts described them as “a high-energy weapon system”.

A Black Hawk helicopter took them to the entrance. They descended through a tunnel and entered a long hallway leading to a T-junction and a horseshoe-shaped passage. The storyteller described a strong, sewer-like smell.

As the team moved around the curved passage, the serviceman on its outer, left-hand side was allegedly struck in the chest by a weapon of the same kind they had been issued. He was killed, and the surviving personnel returned fire.

According to Betts’s retelling, the attacker walked on two legs, looked mildly reptilian, had fingers and was carrying the weapon. The team had allegedly been told there were three beings inside the installation and killed all three.

Asked later in the podcast how many personnel had entered, Betts said the storyteller had not supplied a headcount. He guessed six. 

The storyteller claimed the dead serviceman’s body was cremated immediately. His colleagues allegedly objected because he was Catholic and cremation went against his beliefs. Betts separately said the team had been prevented from taking the body home in a casket, with sterilisation given as the reason it had to remain at the site. His death was said to have been recorded as a training accident.

The surviving personnel allegedly signed documents, had their identification photographed and underwent further biometric scans.

Betts acknowledged that the storyteller had been drinking, telling the hosts:

“He was drunk, but he wasn’t fucking sloppy.”

What happened the next morning, Betts said, was why he took the account seriously.

The group was due to meet in the hotel lobby in the morning. On his way downstairs, Betts encountered the older man whom the storyteller had identified as another participant in the operation.

Betts casually mentioned that their mutual companion had said the older man knew something about aliens.

The man immediately grabbed him by the neck and slammed him against a wall, Betts alleged. He warned Betts never to discuss the subject again, then demanded to know where he had heard the story.

Betts later saw the two men arguing. The storyteller subsequently confronted him and demanded that he leave the country. Betts said neither man would speak to him for the remainder of the trip.

Betts said the fallout cost him the documentary job. He and Ranger were told to pack after breakfast, and he recalled hiding beneath bedsheets and pillows while calling his wife to say he was coming home early.

“I literally got canned off the job,” he said.

He and Ranger were then taken to a facility Betts described as a “black site”, driven to an airport and flown home from Poland. On the flight, he asked Ranger what he made of the incident. His friend replied:

“I think you shut the fuck up about it.”

The hosts suggested the story and confrontation could have been a prank. Betts questioned why a joke would end with him losing his job and thousands of dollars in paid work.

He also acknowledged that discussing the account publicly made him nervous. Asked whether one of the men would be angry to hear him recount it, he replied:

“That’s why I’m nervous.”

His account was published nearly ten months before David Grusch’s appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience on 30 September 2026.

Grusch, the former Air Force intelligence officer who testified before Congress in July 2023, told Rogan that his contacts had described reptilian-looking beings, some more than seven feet tall, with scaly skin and a gorilla-like appearance. He added that others were described as more humanoid in appearance.

He alleged that U.S. personnel had shot living reptilian beings during a crash retrieval, and that Americans had been injured and killed. Asked why the beings were shot, Grusch said:

“It posed a threat.”

Betts and Grusch are not alone in relaying claims about reptilian-looking beings.

In May 2025, Dr Eric W. Davis, a theoretical physicist and former Pentagon contractor, told lawmakers during a multi-panel event that his sources had described beings resembling reptiles among the crews of some UFOs.

Separately, an intelligence community source speaking to Liberation Times described alleged reptile-like beings referred to as “strangers”.

The source described them as aggressive beings based beneath the Moon’s surface and claimed they were competing with a “Nordic” group characterised as more empathetic.

The source did not describe a conventional war:

“Competition between the sides may be nearly as old as humanity itself. What I've heard described isn't an outright war, but rather a scaled-down adversarial relationship.

“It's unclear which sides have aligned with international governments, or which sides are cooperating with factions within the program. It's quite possible that every government has had to manage this competition among the sides.”

The account echoes Grusch’s broader claims on The Joe Rogan Experience of conflict between different non-human groups.
