item.description: Security reports obtained by Liberation Times describe repeated drone flights over Virginia's Surry Nuclear Power Plant in December 2024, including a flight over both reactor containment buildings.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Kyle Warfel and Christopher Sharp - 7 October 2026

  • Liberation Times obtained 67 NRC drone-related reports covering 28 nuclear sites across 17 states, with accounts spanning February 2024 to March 2026.

  • Repeated flights were reported over Surry Nuclear Power Plant, roughly 20 miles from Langley Air Force Base, including one over both reactor containment buildings. A separate account records radar confirmation from nearby Fort Eustis.

  • Surry security described a triangular-looking drone and two smaller drones zigzagging around a larger aircraft before all three disappeared from view.

  • Aircraft estimated to be the size of small cars were reported at New Jersey’s Hope Creek. At Connecticut’s Millstone, security described a five-foot-wide, V-shaped drone that flew over a reactor building.

  • Four drones were reported over Nuclear Fuel Services in Tennessee, which manufactures fuel material for U.S. Navy nuclear reactors. One reportedly appeared to be a ten-foot-by-ten-foot rotary craft.

  • At Haddam Neck’s spent-fuel storage site, security recorded a drone apparently matching the site’s decision to switch off its lights: “When the site turned their lights off, the drone did the same.”

  • Sightings continued into March 2026, and every NRC entry is marked “Closed Unresolved”. The released records provide limited information about subsequent investigations or findings.

  • Separately, police records say the Pentagon classified a manifesto recovered from Matthew Livelsberger’s phone. They do not establish whether it included his emailed allegations about Chinese aircraft using “gravitic propulsion systems”.

Security reports obtained by Liberation Times describe repeated drone flights over Virginia's Surry Nuclear Power Plant in December 2024, including a flight over both reactor containment buildings.

One account describes two smaller drones zigzagging around a larger aircraft before all three disappeared from view.

Another records plant security receiving radar confirmation from nearby Fort Eustis.

The five Surry accounts are among 67 drone-related reports obtained from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) through the Freedom of Information Act.

The NRC is America's civilian nuclear regulator, responsible for licensing, inspection and enforcement of safety and security rules.

The reports cover 28 named nuclear sites across 17 states, with register dates running from 1 February 2024 to 25 March 2026.

They include accounts of drones flying over reactor buildings, spent-fuel storage sites and Nuclear Fuel Services in Tennessee, which manufactures fuel material for the U.S. Navy’s nuclear-powered submarines and aircraft carriers.

An individual report can cover several aircraft or repeated sightings.

Surry sits roughly 20 miles from Langley Air Force Base. Separate Pentagon PHALANX monitoring reports logged 113 drone detection events around Langley that December, including two aircraft tracked about 250 metres outside its boundary.

The two sets of reports do not establish a flight between Surry and Langley or identify a common operator.

A year earlier, incursions over Langley had disrupted F-22 operations and, according to The Wall Street Journal, triggered White House meetings.

Flights Over Surry's Reactors

On 3 December 2024, Surry reported multiple drones passing over its owner-controlled grounds and protected area - the secured part of the site - between 8.45pm and midnight.

The plant heightened security and notified the FBI, local police and Fort Eustis.

An account describing sightings on 10 December records aircraft around security enclosures, the administration building and firing range.

One hovered about 100 feet above a security enclosure before its lights appeared to go out and officers lost sight of it.

Later that evening, an officer saw a larger drone north of the construction area, with red, green and white lights.

While that sighting was being reported, another aircraft passed overhead. An officer described 'a triangular solid appearing shaped drone'.

A third drone moved east from the firing range, hovered near a parking lot and climbed.

The account then describes two smaller aircraft 'flying in a zig zag pattern opposite of each other laterally north to south around the larger drone'.

All three travelled east by northeast before disappearing from view.

The narrative dates the sightings to 10 December, although the register lists 9 December.

Fort Eustis, the Army component of Joint Base Langley-Eustis, sits across the James River from Surry. Plant security contacted it repeatedly during the December sightings.

On 12 December, an off-duty security officer reported a drone near a checkpoint.

According to the NRC report, the Fort Eustis control tower 'confirmed that the drone appeared on radar at approximately 300 feet.'

A Surry County deputy later reported three drones nearby before they crossed into Isle of Wight County.

The next evening, an officer saw a drone above a gate.

It moved west over a crane enclosure and disappeared without entering the protected area. Calls to Fort Eustis and Norfolk Radar Approach Control produced no identification.

On 17 December, another aircraft crossed the protected area and passed over both reactor containment buildings. Fort Eustis air traffic control told Surry there was no military drone activity in the area.

The reports record the plant's account of radar confirmation but include no radar data or images identifying the aircraft.

Drones Detected Near Langley

The separate PHALANX reports came from the Pentagon's Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA).

They were obtained through FOIA and published by Government Attic.

The December 2024 report logged 56 drone serial numbers within about five miles of Langley, generating 113 detection events.

Repeated detections of the same serial number were sometimes grouped into one event, so the figure cannot be read as 113 separate aircraft or base incursions.

On 2 December, PHALANX recorded two aircraft operating about 250 metres west of Langley's boundary. One was identified as a Skydio drone. The other was a DJI aircraft whose activity appeared recreational.

Surry reported multiple drones crossing its owner-controlled and protected areas the following night.

The PHALANX logs identified familiar retail models, including DJI Mini and Mavic drones. Some serial numbers were also detected near Naval Weapons Station Yorktown and Norfolk Naval Shipyard that month.

For Langley itself, the December report states that there were 'no detects occurring within Langley's base boundary.'

That describes what this monitoring recorded; it does not establish that every flight in the area was detected.

The overlap with Surry is in the month and region. Neither set of reports matches an aircraft at one site to the other.

The Swarms That Disrupted Langley

Earlier headline-grabbing Langley incursions occurred in December 2023.

Drones of unknown origin appeared over the base during a 17-day period, with the Air Force confirming that sightings began on 6 December.

Langley houses F-22 fighter units and Air Combat Command's headquarters. Its fighters help defend U.S. airspace, including the skies around Washington, D.C.

The Air Force said the aircraft varied in size and configuration and showed no apparent hostile intent, although their presence in restricted airspace posed a flight-safety risk.

The Wall Street Journal reported that commanders cancelled nighttime training over collision concerns and moved F-22 fighters to another base.

President Joe Biden was briefed, and the incursions prompted two weeks of White House meetings, according to the newspaper.

Liberation Times later obtained 22 witness statements and an incident report from the 633d Security Forces Squadron through FOIA.

One account described 15 to 20 small unmanned aircraft entering and leaving the base between 6.30pm and 11pm on 6 December.

Another witness saw nine moving towards the flight line in a diamond formation.

Security officers struggled to respond. One said a handheld Dronebuster counter-drone device 'failed to register' an object.

In another account, fog and a lack of visual contact prevented its use.

NASA's WB-57 research aircraft also supported the response, The War Zone reported.

NASA confirmed that its aircraft provided additional imaging support in Virginia that December. Its public schedule lists imaging work on 18 and 19 December without identifying the mission's subject.

In March 2024, General Gregory Guillot, then commanding the North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) and U.S. Northern Command, told the Senate that the counter-drone mission had dominated his first month in command. He was using the Langley-Eustis events as the centrepiece of his 90-day assessment.

At a House hearing on 29 April 2025, Rear Admiral Paul Spedero Jr., the Joint Staff's vice director for operations, described them as 'the longest and the largest series of incursions that we have seen to date.'

At the same hearing, acting Assistant Secretary of Defense Mark Ditlevson said internal difficulties and a relatively untested process for coordinating with other agencies had hampered the response.

He also said the department had since improved its procedures and responses.

Surry's Place in the Earlier Investigation

Surry had already featured in Liberation Times' investigation of the 2023 Langley events.

Civilian, Jonathan Butner, said he was stargazing from the western bank of the James River on 14 December 2023 when he saw approximately 40 blinking, car-sized objects over Langley.

He also described a larger, saucer-shaped object passing Newport News and travelling 'towards Fort Eustis before then circling by Surry Nuclear Power Plant.'

Butner said he gave footage and testimony to the FBI.

The footage published with Liberation Times' May 2024 reporting does not clearly show the shapes he described.

At the time of that reporting, the Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) said it had received no report or information about the Langley incident.

Butner's account and Surry's proximity to Langley prompted Liberation Times to ask the NRC on 3 May 2024 whether the plant had reported drone activity the previous December and whether it was being investigated.

NRC spokesperson David McIntyre replied on 8 May 2024:

'The NRC regulations in 10 CFR Part 73 require licensees to notify the NRC of suspicious activity at licensed facilities. Until January 2024, reporting of drone sightings was voluntary, and we did not receive a report from Surry on the dates you specified.

‘The NRC regulations now require reporting of drone flyovers within posted or restricted areas and within close proximity to the facility (i.e., above or near).'

Car-Sized Aircraft Reported at Hope Creek

The NRC reports describe sightings at other nuclear sites during December 2024, including New Jersey's Hope Creek Nuclear Generating Station.

On 13 December, security watched two drones leave its protected area. The report states:

'Both drones were 400 feet in the air with red and white flashing lights and were approximately the size of a small motor vehicle.'

Three drones were reported inside the protected area the following evening. A larger craft hovered near the cooling tower, then entered the area near two smaller drones above Unit 1.

Local police responded. The account also states:

'The FBI opened an active investigation into the drone sightings.'

It provides no subsequent findings from that investigation.

Descriptions of size, shape and altitude in these reports are observers' estimates, rather than independent technical identifications.

Flights Over Reactors and Spent-Fuel Sites

At Connecticut's Millstone Power Station, security reported seven drones on 14 December 2024, describing them as quadcopters about three feet by three feet with flashing green and red lights. Two briefly entered the protected area.

At about 1.30am the following morning, another aircraft appeared near the spent-fuel storage facility. Security described 'a large (5 ft. across), V-shaped drone'.

As officers approached the fence for a better view, it flew west over the Unit 2 reactor building and departed over Niantic Bay.

Millstone kept its security posture unchanged during and after both incidents.

Louisiana's River Bend Station accounts for ten of the 67 reports, the largest total for any named site in the collection.

On 6 January 2025, security saw about five drones roughly 100 feet above its reactor building.

The report records:

'The drones appeared as rectangular and black. No lights were observed.'

They disappeared from view to the south four minutes later.

Security heightened its awareness and notified the sheriff's department, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the FBI.

Two days later, four drones were reported around Minnesota's Prairie Island station. They covered all four quadrants of the owner-controlled area and crossed into the protected area about twice.

Security adopted an elevated posture. Police responded but could not identify the operators. The drones left about 44 minutes after the initial report, and security stood down.

An earlier report describes an aircraft approaching California's Diablo Canyon from over the ocean on 25 October 2024.

Security activated a “Code Yellow” alert, indicating a heightened state of security awareness. The craft spent approximately five minutes inside the protected area.

The aircraft was described as two to three feet in size, with small wings and multiple amber lights. An officer said it was 'extremely quiet with no buzzing sound present.'

Security cameras revealed no operators. Attempts to identify the aircraft failed; details of those attempts are redacted.

Lights Go Out as Sightings Continue

The accounts extend well beyond December 2024.

At Connecticut's Haddam Neck spent-fuel storage site, a report dated 27 March 2025 describes four drones circling around and inside the perimeter.

One was larger than the other three. They flew at about 200 to 300 feet, sometimes higher, and were still over the site when the report was made two hours later.

The next evening, security saw an aircraft about the size of a folding table fly west over the site and then reverse direction. The officers recorded:

'When the site turned their lights off, the drone did the same.'

The site's security posture remained unchanged.

At Nuclear Fuel Services in Tennessee, security reported four drones over the facility on 23 May 2025, between 11.10pm and 11.43pm.

Its parent company, BWXT, says the facility manufactures fuel material for naval reactors used in U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers.

The report states:

'All sighted drones displayed navigation lights and one appeared to be a 10x10 ft rotary craft.'

A review of footage revealed a similar aircraft had flown over the site on 18 May, travelling west to east at 300 feet or below without loitering.

Further sightings followed on 3 June, when several apparent quadcopters were still near the facility as the report was made.

At Illinois' Clinton station, officers saw four to five drones circling near the flume discharge area on 12 September 2025. Three returned after a brief departure and resumed the same flight patterns.

Two more were reported near that area on 14 September. A separate sighting followed over the protected area.

An officer tracked an aircraft over the raw water treatment building and lake, then 'lost visual as it appeared the drone lights shut off near the route 54 bridge.'

The Haddam Neck and Clinton reports do not explain why the lights appeared to go out.

Sightings Continue Into 2026

The most recent NRC reports describe activity in 2026.

On 9 February, a contracted employee reported a drone over the north end of Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island. Site security and state police responded but did not see the aircraft.

At Illinois' Byron Nuclear Station, the latest account began at about 11.10pm on 24 March 2026.

Staff saw a drone cross the protected area from northwest to southeast. The FBI's Rockford office, FAA air traffic control and the Ogle County Sheriff's Department were contacted.

At 12.08am on 25 March, security officers and police observed two separate drones over the owner-controlled and protected areas.

The report states:

'Drone activity continued until 0130.'

The sightings spanned roughly two hours and 20 minutes.

Langley Questions and a Classified Manifesto

Questions about responsibility for the 2023 Langley incursions have continued on Capitol Hill.

In a 24 September 2026 interview for Ask a Pol, journalist Matt Laslo asked Senator Mike Rounds about a source's claim that China had caused the 17-day disruption and relocation of F-22 fighters.

Rounds, a South Dakota Republican, sits on the Senate Intelligence Committee.

'I can't talk about that right now,' Rounds replied.

Asked whether the United States possessed comparable technology, he said:

'Let's put it this way, they don't keep me or members of our [Intelligence] Committee awake at night. But I suspect we keep them awake at night.'

A separate allegation about Chinese aircraft came from Army Special Forces soldier Matthew Livelsberger, who died in the Cybertruck explosion outside the Trump International Hotel in Las Vegas on 1 January 2025.

On 31 December 2024, Livelsberger sent retired Army intelligence officer Sam Shoemate a manifesto by email.

Made public on the Shawn Ryan Show on 3 January 2025, the manifesto alleged that East Coast sightings involved Chinese aircraft using 'gravitic propulsion systems'.

He claimed both China and the United States possessed that capability.

Authorities later confirmed that Livelsberger had sent the emailed manifesto, ABC News reported.

Days after the emailed manifesto became public, the Pentagon classified a manifesto recovered from Livelsberger’s phone.

The Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department’s after-action report, published in November 2025, dates that decision to 9 January 2025:

'The U.S. Department of Defense declared the manifesto classified, and the investigation was turned over to the federal government.'

The report also records that police were told they could no longer disclose further information about the recovered manifesto.

A police announcement published on 8 January 2025 described the recovered manifesto as 'in addition to' the email and two previously published letters.

However, neither the announcement nor the later report establishes whether the recovered document included the emailed manifesto or its drone allegations. The report does not identify the material that led to classification.

What the NRC Reports Leave Unanswered

Every NRC entry carries the status 'Closed Unresolved'. 

Many narratives also say the reports are open pending internal review. The documents do not explain that discrepancy, and neither label establishes the current status of investigations by the FBI, FAA or police.

Not every sighting was assessed as suspicious.

Quad Cities security reached that conclusion about sightings on 1 and 2 February 2024. At California's Rancho Seco spent-fuel site, a 25 June 2024 flyover received the same assessment based on its flight path and pattern.

At Maine Yankee, officers saw an individual take pictures or video outside the entrance and launch a drone on 10 August 2024.

The person ignored announcements to leave, recovered the aircraft and drove away in an SUV. Police could not intercept them.

The NRC's Inspector General has examined the broader issue. Its April to September 2025 semiannual report recorded 34 suspicious-activity reports involving unauthorised drones between 10 August 2024 and 11 January 2025 - a shorter period than the reports obtained by Liberation Times.

The review examined the NRC's response, oversight and coordination with other agencies. It said most specifics involved sensitive information protected in the interest of national security.

A rule published in March 2023 set 8 January 2024 as the compliance deadline for relevant new security-reporting requirements.

The NRC's January 2025 fact sheet said nuclear plant operators must report drone sightings over their facilities.

The same fact sheet said plant security forces lacked authority to intercept or shoot down aircraft, including drones. It stressed that nuclear plants have hardened structures, armed personnel, physical barriers and surveillance systems.

Liberation Times' earlier reporting on Coast Guard records documented December 2024 sightings off New Jersey. Those records also included a TSA assessment attributing some footage to conventional aircraft approaching JFK. 

Across more than two years, the nuclear-site reports document repeated sightings, flights over protected areas and calls to law enforcement. They offer far less information about what happened after those calls. 

The latest Byron account records aircraft still being sighted at 1.30am, but gives no subsequent findings about their operators or purpose.

Allegations of Chinese involvement in the separate Langley incursions raise concerns about possible surveillance of sensitive nuclear infrastructure by a foreign power.

The sightings also invite comparison with a much longer history of reported Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena encounters around nuclear facilities, including a former security officer’s account of a triangular object over Cooper Nuclear Station in the 1980s and Australian government records of UFO sightings near a nuclear weapons testing range in 1960.

The released NRC reports neither link the Surry flights to China nor establish a connection with those historical accounts.

For the unidentified aircraft reported over reactor buildings, the central questions remain unanswered: who was flying them, whether they were gathering intelligence, and what investigators established after the plant alerted federal authorities.

The latest findings build on Liberation Times’ April 2026 investigation, which revealed 22 drone-related incidents around U.S. nuclear facilities between September 2022 and February 2023.

Those records included a prolonged incursion at Pennsylvania’s Susquehanna nuclear plant involving multiple aircraft, one described as a larger triangular object apparently carrying a spotlight.

item.title: White House Leaves UFO Shootdown Claims Unanswered
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: If the White House’s UFO disclosure effort ends here, the gatekeepers can breathe easy. Much of the imagery released under PURSUE remains too ambiguous to settle the questions it raises, leaving plenty of room for online argument.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 26 September 2026

If the White House’s UFO disclosure effort ends here, the gatekeepers can breathe easy.

Much of the imagery released under PURSUE remains too ambiguous to settle the questions it raises, leaving plenty of room for online argument. 

Many of the other documents have been seen before.

Release of any groundbreaking footage has been hindered. 

Two videos allegedly showing a 100-foot triangular UFO over a Colorado military base were said to be held by the Air Force Office of Special Investigations. Sources gave the New York Post file numbers for the videos as IRR1669S015524 and IRR1669S005024.

However, the Pentagon says it cannot find the footage. Deputy Press Secretary Joel Valdez wrote on X:

‘After conducting a thorough records review, the Department of War did not find any footage pertaining to the alleged sighting in question.’

Since July, the Department of War has not provided a substantive answer to Liberation Times’ questions about an alleged operation to lure UFOs, otherwise known as Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP), at a sensitive U.S. testing facility.

Journalist Ross Coulthart went one step further.

He claimed that the Department of War had been authorized by President Trump to engage with UFOs and had downed objects in the U.S. and Juárez in Mexico - across the border from El Paso.

Liberation Times put this allegation to the Department of War. An official responded, stating:

“We refer you to the White House regarding any orders, directives, or authorization issues by President Trump.”

Liberation Times put Coulthart’s claim directly to the White House. We asked:

‘Has President Trump, as Commander-in-Chief, issued any order, directive or authorization permitting U.S. military personnel to shoot down UAP, UFOs, unidentified “orbs” or other unidentified airborne objects?’

We also asked whether the government had carried out an operation to lure UAP.

On Tuesday 22 September, the White House’s press office asked for our deadline. We set the deadline for 5pm Eastern Time on Friday 25 September. Despite follow-up emails, no response has been provided since the deadline elapsed.

This is not the only frustration, despite the White House’s pledge for transparency.

Harvard professor Avi Loeb was asked by U.S. government agencies to establish a UAP Science Advisory Council.

Its role is to advise the government on UAP research and analyse unclassified evidence.

Yet, as POLITICO reports, the council has received no meaningful data from the government. Loeb may reassess the situation if that does not change by the end of 2026.

The POLITICO article, through its sources, singles out the CIA as the agency most resistant to releasing UAP data.

An intelligence community source told Liberation Times that the agency would continue to protect its sources, collection methods and analytical tools. Those capabilities serve many intelligence missions beyond UAP analysis.

The source said relevant data could come from space-based systems or maritime platforms, with agencies including the NRO, CIA and DIA involved. In their view, the CIA is unlikely to release such data until the systems used to collect it are obsolete.

But in defense of the agency, the source claimed that the CIA has released UFO-related documents in line with declassification schedules. 

Where does this leave the push for UFO disclosure?

Representatives Tim Burchett and Eric Burlison have accused federal agencies of withholding UFO records and frustrating the White House’s efforts to release them.

Yet the White House has not answered Liberation Times’ questions about the alleged luring operation or Coulthart’s claim that President Trump authorised the military to engage unidentified objects.

Several explanations remain possible.

The administration may not be committed to fuller disclosure. Any luring and shootdown activity may have led to unintended consequences. Trump may be unable to get agencies to cooperate. Or he may be holding back information for a larger announcement. Liberation Times understands that some people close to Trump believe he will become a disclosure president. 

For now, the alleged UAP shootdowns remain unverified.

If U.S. forces are engaging unidentified objects, who decides what they are and whether to fire? What safeguards protect civilian aircraft? 

Documented counter-drone activity and aviation incidents near El Paso and White Sands show why those questions matter.

Here is the timeline of noteworthy events connected to White Sands, El Paso and UFOs since late 2025. They paint an interesting picture:

  • Late 2025: At an unidentified U.S. testing facility, a senior intelligence official, helicopter crew and ground personnel reported glowing orbs near a helicopter and fighter jets. The FBI later interviewed the official. The facility has not been officially identified as White Sands, and the claim that the objects were deliberately lured there remains unconfirmed

  • 8–10 February - sightings reported in El Paso: Enigma Labs logged three witness accounts from El Paso, south of White Sands. They described rapidly moving glowing orbs, a large hovering object and four slowly moving round objects.

  • 10–11 February - El Paso airspace closed: The Federal Aviation Administration halted flights at El Paso International Airport, south of White Sands, initially announcing a ten-day restriction. It lifted the closure after roughly eight hours. The administration cited cartel drones, while reporting identified safety concerns over a nearby counter-drone laser

  • 19 February 2026 - Trump announces UFO file review: President Trump said he would direct Secretary Pete Hegseth and other agencies to identify and release government files concerning UFOs, UAP and extraterrestrial life

  • 26 February - second border airspace closure: A military counter-drone system shot down a Customs and Border Protection drone near Fort Hancock, about 50 miles southeast of El Paso and farther from White Sands. The FAA restricted flights in the area

  • 27 February - former laser program director goes missing: Retired Air Force Major General Neil McCasland was reported missing from his home in Albuquerque. He had directed the Air Force’s Space-Based Laser program and later served as technology director at Applied Technology Associates when it unveiled LOCUST, the counter-drone laser identified in reporting on the El Paso closure. Applied Technology Associates became part of BlueHalo in 2020, and was brought under AeroVironment when it acquired BlueHalo in 2025

  • 7–8 March - laser safety tests at White Sands: The military and FAA tested counter-drone lasers at the range

  • 10 April - new laser agreement: Following the White Sands tests, the FAA and Pentagon announced an agreement on using counter-drone lasers along the southwest border

  • 6 May - Fort Bliss chosen for laser pilot: Following counter-drone laser tests at White Sands, the Department of War selected Fort Bliss as one of five bases for a directed-energy counter-drone pilot program. The announcement did not specify which laser would be used at each base

  • 8 May 2026 - PURSUE launches: The Department of War began publishing UAP records through the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE), with support from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

  • 14 May - fatal crash within White Sands GPS advisory area: A medical aircraft crashed near Ruidoso, northeast of the range, killing four people. Its crew had reported losing GPS capability while military GPS interference was active in an area centred on White Sands

  • 19 June - sighting reported in El Paso: A single witness south of White Sands reported a bright, disc-shaped light that appeared to move rapidly and vanish

  • 23 June – Hegseth operates LOCUST at White Sands: During a weapons demonstration at the range, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth operated a LOCUST laser and brought down a drone, according to its manufacturer

  • 9 August 2026 - Coulthart alleges UAP shootdowns: Journalist Ross Coulthart claimed President Trump had authorised a Department of War operation to intercept unidentified objects around White Sands. He said sources told him objects had been downed in the U.S. and near Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, across the border from El Paso

  • 2 September – Army orders more LOCUST systems: AeroVironment announced a $464.8 million Army contract to supply dozens of LOCUST X3 lasers. It said the award followed LOCUST’s tests at White Sands and the subsequent FAA–Pentagon safety agreement

  • 6 September - El Paso sighting claim: A witness south of White Sands reported a pulsing light and said an orb had travelled towards Ciudad Juárez. Video circulated with the account, but the alleged orb was reportedly seen before the recorded segment

  • 9–19 September - GPS interference advisory: The FAA warned pilots of scheduled testing centred on White Sands that could make GPS signals unreliable or unavailable across a wide area

Liberation Times has previously reported allegations about a program named Golden Domes. A source claimed it used electronic and laser-based systems to bring down what the source described as ‘exotic non-human vehicles’. The source said former Director of National Intelligence James Clapper and his principal deputy, Stephanie O’Sullivan, oversaw the program.

O’Sullivan also chaired a CIA board that examined a documented program involving aircraft shootdowns. 

A CIA inspector general’s report records several shootdowns under the U.S.-supported Airbridge Denial Program in Peru, including one on 23 March 1997. It sets out the warnings and authorisation required before firing on suspected drug-trafficking aircraft, and finds repeated failures to follow those procedures. O’Sullivan’s board later recommended administrative penalties for 16 officers.

The March 1997 shootdown occurred around the time former Marine Jonathan Weygandt claims he encountered a retrieved UFO while deployed to Peru for Operation Laser Strike, a related counter-drug effort.

The consequences of a mistaken shootdown became clear on 20 April 2001.

A Peruvian Air Force jet misidentified a civilian missionary plane as a drug-trafficking aircraft and fired on it, killing a woman and her infant daughter.

U.S. support for air interdiction operations in Peru and Colombia was suspended.

The case is a reminder that mistakes in identifying aircraft, or failures to follow safeguards, can cost innocent lives.

That is why the White House should answer whether U.S. forces have been authorised to engage unidentified objects and, if so, what safeguards protect civilian aircraft.

item.title: The Kammler Connection: The Nazi SS General at the Center of an Alleged U.S. UFO Legacy Program
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: Did SS General Hans Kammler die in 1945, or enter American custody? Intelligence Community sources say his fate may connect an alleged 1933 Italian recovery to a postwar American UFO legacy program.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 12 September 2026

Did SS General Hans Kammler die in 1945, or enter American custody?

Intelligence Community sources allege that he became a key link between Nazi efforts to exploit recovered technology and a postwar American UFO legacy program. The claim is extraordinary.

The documented reasons the United States might have wanted him are not.

What the sources allege:

  • Italy recovered a craft near Magenta in 1933, gave Germany access in 1934 and identified its occupants as advanced terrestrial “Nordics”

  • Himmler’s 1935 Ahnenerbe became the program used to find the “Nordics” and exploit their technology

  • The United States learned of the work in 1944-45. The sources say it later absorbed an overt von Braun stream and a covert Kammler stream through the Joint Intelligence Objectives Agency, Overcast and Paperclip

  • They trace the work through the CIG, CIA and Air Force, then to a claimed 1962 transfer into the Air Force and defense industry

  • The Magenta account recasts the Die Glocke legend. Any Bell-like device, they say, may have been an attempt to copy recovered technology

  • The central historical question is whether Kammler survived and entered American custody.

The Paper That Changes The Question

On a typewritten page dated 7 May 1945, Hans Kammler appears not as a fugitive or a dead man, but as a prisoner being sent for interrogation.

The page was reproduced in the 2019 book The Hidden Nazi. It identifies the SS-Obergruppenführer as responsible for Germany’s V-weapons and secret projects.

It says he surrendered on 6 May and was being sent to Kohnstein for “detailed interrogation and evaluation” of underground weapons research.

The copy is difficult to authenticate. It has no traceable file number or identified archival original. Its letterhead and signature are redacted. But other American and British records also cast doubt on Kammler’s accepted death.

Even without Magenta or Die Glocke, Kammler had plenty to offer. By 1945, he sat above secret weapons, underground factories, engineers and records. If the Americans got him, they got a map to part of the hidden Reich.

Germany was not ahead in every field. But it had pushed further than the Allies in several areas of military technology, including ballistic missiles, operational jet aircraft, guided weapons and high-speed aerodynamics.

For the United States, capturing that knowledge could accelerate its own weapons programs. It could also deny the same scientists, documents and hardware to the Soviet Union.

The Engineer Of Weapons - And Mass Murder

To understand Kammler’s value, it is first necessary to understand what he controlled - and the crimes on which that power was built.

A 29 January 1943 letter addressed to Kammler reported progress on Crematorium II at Birkenau and referred to its basement “gassing cellar”.

The Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum records that he authorized three undressing barracks beside provisional gas chambers during the 1944 murder of Hungarian Jews.

Children were among the victims. The Auschwitz Museum estimates that about 232,000 children and young people were deported to the camp. Most were killed.

Forced labour also powered Kammler’s weapons system.

The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum calls him the “decisive personality” in the history of Mittelbau.

In a word, Kammler was evil. There is no glamour to Kammler and his deeds.

Prisoners dug tunnels and assembled V-2 rockets in appalling conditions.

More than 20,000 people died across the camp system.

By the final months of the war, Kammler’s special staff controlled or coordinated underground A-4 production, V-weapons and priority aircraft programs.

He sat above specialists such as Wernher von Braun, whose team developed the V-2 for the Nazis and later the Saturn V for the Americans.

Kammler had become a systems manager of Nazi secrecy. He knew who was doing what, where work and records were hidden, and how the compartments fitted together.

One researcher who wishes to remain anonymous and has extensive knowledge of the Kammler mystery and German technology research during World War 2 told Liberation Times:

“[Kammler] would have been exceptionally valuable because he was probably the only person who held most, if not all, of the knowledge of all the secret compartments of all the V-weapons in his head.”

A September 1946 British assessment was more cautious. It said Kammler’s technical knowledge might be second-hand, but that he knew where documents, stocks and pilot plants could be found.

That was already bargaining power. Any exotic technology, if it existed within his network, would only have added to it.

The Race For German Technology

The scale of that value becomes clearer in the final weeks of the war. German science had become an American military objective.

On 25 April 1945, General Carl Spaatz said Operation LUSTY - the U.S. Army Air Forces hunt for German aeronautical technology - had “equal priority with operations”.

The National Museum of the U.S. Air Force says teams collected aircraft, weapons and documents, inspected research sites and recruited scientists.

That technology hunt unfolded alongside the final military campaign. General George Patton wanted to continue toward Berlin. But Eisenhower, Supreme Allied Commander in Europe, chose not to make the capital the principal Western objective.

In mid-April, Patton’s Third Army was directed southeast through southern Germany toward Austria.

Allied fears of a Nazi “National Redoubt” in the Alps were part of the calculation.

The route still carried U.S. forces through some of the Reich’s most sensitive infrastructure.

The Third Army entered the Ohrdruf area near the secret S-3 complex at Jonastal and captured the underground cache at Merkers.

Elsewhere, American forces reached Nordhausen and the Kohnstein tunnels, where V-2 production had moved from Peenemünde. They seized parts for around 100 V-2s before the area passed to Soviet control.

German researchers had scattered too.

Wernher von Braun was sent south to Bavaria and surrendered to U.S. forces. Specialist teams raced across Germany and Austria for hardware, files, laboratories and scientists before the Soviets could reach them.

The Americans were racing for the Reich’s technology. Kammler could have offered something even more useful: the route map.

That is the setting for one of the most intriguing claims about his final days.

The Hidden Nazi records Kammler’s wife telling their son Jörg that “the Americans reached out to Kammler, not the reverse.”

If the family account is accurate, contact may have begun before the war ended.

The Story Before Roswell

The sources speaking to Liberation Times place a far more extraordinary story inside that documented hunt.

Their chronology begins fourteen years before Roswell - the July 1947 incident in New Mexico that became central to the history of alleged U.S. UFO recovery.

They allege that an unusual craft was recovered near Magenta in 1933, during Benito Mussolini’s rule.

They say human-looking bodies found with it belonged to an advanced, Earth-based population they call “Nordics”, rather than extraterrestrial visitors.

Germany, they say, gained access in 1934 and began exploiting the technology with Italy. Open-source evidence of close German-Italian research that early is scarce. Technical cooperation grew later.

By 1943, Germany occupied northern Italy and controlled key military and industrial sites. One was SIAI-Marchetti at Vergiate, near Milan. Italian UFO researcher Roberto Pinotti identifies it as the likely storage site for the alleged wreckage.

Former U.S. intelligence official David Grusch brought part of the Magenta story into public view in June 2023.

In a recorded interview, he said a craft recovered near Magenta in 1933 was later secured by the United States. He also alleged that the Vatican helped American officials locate it.

Grusch did not mention bodies.

That claim comes from the Intelligence Community sources speaking to Liberation Times.

Italian citizen Marco Negri described a separate family story: his great-great-grandfather, Pietro Negri - Podesta (Mayor) of Arona - spoke of a wingless metallic aircraft crashing in Magenta in the 1930s, with two blond-haired “bodies” inside.

In the sources’ chronology, Magenta is the recovery point. The next link is institutional. They say Germany formalised the search through Heinrich Himmler’s creation of the SS Ahnenerbe in 1935.

The Alleged German Program

The SS Ahnenerbe existed. We know that, at the very least.

Founded by Heinrich Himmler in 1935, it used archaeology, anthropology and expeditions to support Nazi racial ideas.

The sources say it also concealed another mission: finding the terrestrial “Nordic” population and obtaining its technology.

The sources call the alleged technology “Vril”, a term from Edward Bulwer-Lytton’s 1871 novel The Coming Race. The novel revolves around an advanced subterranean race with telepathic powers, known as Vril-ya.

Later occult writers treated Vril as real.

The sources say Kammler’s absorbed team later spoke of “Vril craft”.

For that claim to connect with Kammler, the Ahnenerbe and his secret-weapons apparatus need to intersect.

And bizarrely, they do.

Ahnenerbe, Kammler And The S-3 Gap

Hans Schleif provides the clearest bridge. He was an architect and archaeologist who had led Ahnenerbe excavations before handing the post to Herbert Jankuhn in the summer of 1942.

On 14 April 1943, Ahnenerbe manager Wolfram Sievers asked Kammler to use Schleif in the SS construction apparatus.

Kammler agreed two days later.

Schleif entered the SS-WVHA in 1943 and, by mid-1944, was one of Kammler’s deputies. Julian Klein’s study cites the Bundesarchiv letters.

A second, less certain bridge comes from military historian Tino Struckmann. In his documentary ‘SS Ahnenerbe’, he says he found Kammler-to-Himmler memoranda about secret research locations for the organization.

In Struckmann’s words:

“The head of the special weapons program [Kammler] was working on locations for them [the SS Ahnenerbe].”

Struckmann also cites Werner Goldmann’s account of Ahnenerbe officers at the highly secret S-3 complex in the Jonastal.

Postwar accounts link the site to secret-weapons testing and nuclear research.

The overlap between what is seen as a fringe pseudoscience group and the Nazi’s complex secret weapons development is striking.

Later UFO accounts echo the archaeological theme associated with the Ahnenerbe.

Dylan Borland alleged that an advanced vehicle of unknown origin was unearthed during a dig. Bob Lazar said in 2019 that he recalled a UAP linked to an archaeological excavation.

The Ahnenerbe’s wartime interests also reached into marine research.

Historian Maria Zarifi found that the German-Greek Biological Institute in occupied Piraeus took part in marine-science programs conducted by staff working under Walther Wüst, the scientific head of the SS Ahnenerbe.

German researchers were also carrying out oceanographic work across the Aegean for military authorities.

Separately, German divers in occupied Greece were conducting underwater scientific work and recovering archaeological material.

The Bell Legend

The wider Nazi-UFO literature is notoriously difficult to disentangle from postwar invention, and many of its best-known claims lack contemporary documentation.

That is why Die Glocke matters here. Not because its existence has been established, but because it became the best-known story placing exotic propulsion inside Kammler’s secret-weapons world.

In modern UFO and alternative-history circles, Kammler is tied to Die Glocke - “The Bell”.

Aviation journalist Nick Cook popularised the claim in his 2001 book The Hunt for Zero Point, after Igor Witkowski’s Prawda o Wunderwaffe.

Cook described a glowing, rotating machine said to consume enormous power and produce an antigravity effect.

Witkowski said a Polish official showed him secret papers. They have never surfaced, and no Allied capture record identifies the Bell.

Cook proposed that Kammler might have traded the device, or knowledge of it, for his freedom. That helped cement the modern link between Kammler, exotic propulsion and an American deal.

The Kammler connection later surfaced in Tom DeLonge’s Sekret Machines: Chasing Shadows.

Although a novel, DeLonge has described the project as informed by contacts within the U.S. defence and intelligence worlds.

The story explicitly depicts Kammler surviving the war and connects his secret-weapons apparatus to Die Glocke, underground research and the subsequent American exploitation of German technology.

Although not independent corroboration, the parallels with what Liberation Times sources are alleging is eyecatching.

The anonymous researcher who spoke with Liberation Times suggested that stories of Nazi-built flying saucers may have obscured the recovery of a craft Germany did not build:

“Maybe the Nazis did recover some form of alien crashed craft, and that was recovered by the Americans at the end of the war - and therefore all of those stories about the Nazis building flying saucers were a kind of smokescreen, a false trail to obscure what really happened.”

Whether the Bell existed does not decide the Kammler case.

His documented value stands without it. The more concrete question is whether the man himself survived.

Did Kammler Die?

The conventional account rests on conflicting testimony about a suicide near Prague. No body or personal effects were recovered.

A Berlin court nevertheless declared Kammler dead as of 9 May 1945 after his widow petitioned for the ruling. The decision established a legal death. It did not produce a body.

If Kammler instead entered American custody, that ruling would have made him easier to disappear from the record. That remains speculation. The harder problem is what appears in later files.

What The 7 May Paper Actually Says

The disputed page that opened this article is the most dramatic piece of that puzzle.

The Hidden Nazi says Holocaust historian Professor Gerald Fleming supplied the page after years of requests from co-author Colm Lowery.

Marked “By Diplomatic Pouch”, it says Kammler surrendered on 6 May and was to be taken to Kohnstein. A Counter Intelligence Corps officer, it adds, held documents from him that “may prove to be of considerable value”.

The page is not an original from a named archive. Much is blacked out. It has no traceable file number, and its letterhead and signature are redacted.

The report reads:

“Dr. Ing. KAMMLER is a trained architect by profession and was head of all secret projects including the V-1 and V-2. He further claims to have been head of [redacted] project based at the [redacted].

CIC Officer is in possession of documents from KAMMLER which may prove to be of considerable value. Dr. KAMMLER surrendered 6 May with other named persons attached.

Dressed in Heer uniform he later identified himself to an officer of [redacted]. By way of special order KAMMLER is to be transferred immediately to KOHNSTEIN, Germany for purposes of detailed interrogation and evaluation of underground weapons research and production facilities.

At the suggestion of the investigating officers Kammler is preparing a detailed report (in German). This is to include the following: Secret weapons development [redacted] Underground research and production facilities.”

The Dead Man In The American Files

The 7 May page is not the end of the trail. Later records are harder to square with a bureaucracy that had simply written Kammler off as dead.

A U.S. Strategic Air Forces memorandum dated 30 May 1945 listed German air personnel “presently being held for interrogation”. Kammler appears as number 18.

The Wilson Center investigation cites the document to the U.S. Air Force Historical Research Agency.

On 2 November 1945, Brigadier General George C. McDonald ordered personal interrogations of Albert Speer, Karl-Otto Saur and Kammler about underground installations. He called it the highest priority.

British files add another reference.

In September 1946, officers considered the danger that the Soviets might obtain Kammler’s knowledge of hidden documents, stocks and pilot plants.

No Paperclip file bearing Kammler’s name has been released, nor a completed American interrogation.

But his fate no longer turns on the disputed 7 May page alone. If U.S. agencies held him, the next question is whether they would have been prepared to hide it.

What America Was Prepared To Conceal

A secret arrangement with Kammler would have been politically toxic. His crimes alone gave Washington a reason to keep any relationship out of public view.

The anonymous researcher believes that is why he would have remained outside the formal Paperclip system:

“My understanding was that [Kammler] wasn't part of Paperclip. . . . There was another category that didn't even make Paperclip because their past was so unsavory, and Kammler fell into that bracket because he effectively was one of the architects of the Holocaust.”

There are documented cases in which utility overrode policy. A National Archives investigation found that Paperclip officials sought rewritten security reports when valuable candidates were barred by Truman’s rules.

Arthur Rudolph, a former Mittelwerk manager who later directed NASA’s Saturn V program, left the United States after a Justice Department investigation.

U.S. officers also protected Gestapo official Klaus Barbie and arranged his escape. Although such cases do not establish a Kammler deal, they do show that usefulness could outweigh a Nazi past.

The sources say the United States absorbed more than useful personnel.

They allege it also inherited Kammler’s compartmentalised secrecy: each participant saw only a task, while ordinary files never revealed the whole.

In their account, that structure allowed the work to move across agencies and contractors without appearing as one continuous program.

The Alleged Route Into The American System

Here, the sources’ chronology moves from Kammler’s fate to the alleged handover.

They trace hidden work through real postwar institutions, arguing that the program survived by changing homes.

They say U.S. officials learned of Magenta and Germany’s exploitation effort in 1944-45.

Liberation Times previously reported that three sources linked the recovery to the OSS and the McGregor Project, a mission tied to Italy’s surrender. A wartime message confirms McGregor moved to the OSS Research and Development Branch in June 1944.

After Germany fell, the Joint Intelligence Objectives Agency became one of the main U.S. mechanisms for exploiting German expertise.

The National Archives says it operated under the Joint Chiefs and ran the foreign-scientist program, first called Overcast and later Paperclip.

Its documented work covered scientists, dossiers and technical intelligence.

The sources allege a second track inside that effort. Von Braun’s rocket team was handled openly.

Kammler’s SS Wunderwaffe personnel, records and technology, they say, were absorbed covertly.

The intelligence structure was also changing.

When the OSS broke up, its Research and Analysis Branch moved to the Department of State, where its lineage led to the Bureau of Intelligence and Research.

Clandestine elements continued as the War Department’s Strategic Services Unit, then moved into the Central Intelligence Group.

The sources say those successor bodies preserved an SS technology-exploitation effort, including covert activity in Latin America.

In January 1946, President Harry Truman established the National Intelligence Authority, the CIG and the position of Director of Central Intelligence.

The sources say this structure oversaw covert operations tied to the SS effort in Latin America.

A further transfer followed in 1947.

Secretary of War Robert Patterson approved moving the Manhattan Engineer District’s intelligence and counterintelligence unit to the CIG.

A top-secret State Department directive records the transfer of its Foreign Intelligence Branch, personnel and files. The sources say it fed the CIG’s Office of Special Operations.

The sources make a larger claim about the same year. They say SS craft exploitation helped drive both an autonomous intelligence agency able to act abroad - including support for military dictatorships in Latin America - and a separate aerospace-focused armed service.

For context of the Nazi presence in Argentina following the war, a U.S. State Department report declared:

“In Argentina the Germans have constructed a complete duplicate of the economic structure for war which they had in Germany… a base for the reconstitution of German aggressive power.”  

The July 1947 National Security Act created the framework for the National Military Establishment, CIA and independent Air Force.

The structure took effect that September. The National Military Establishment became the Department of Defense in August 1949.

The sources say the hidden effort helped drive those changes.

For 1948-49, they point to the Office of Air Research at Wright Field, the Armed Services Procurement Act, the CIA Act of 1949 and the CIA’s Office of Scientific Intelligence.

They say these supplied research, contracting and secrecy authorities. Analyst, Kit Green, later joined the biological and medical side of CIA scientific intelligence.

The chronology then jumps to the Kennedy era.

The sources say a Wunderwaffe-derived stream stayed separate from the public space program until 1962.

They identify Harald Malmgren as a CIA non-official-cover officer and allege that he briefed President Kennedy in 1961 about JIOA.

That briefing, they say, included claims from Kammler’s team about “Vril” craft and SS beliefs linked to the Vril Society.

They say Kennedy shut JIOA down in 1962 and the program passed to defense contractors and the Air Force.

The National Archives confirms that JIOA was disbanded in 1962 and its functions moved into the Pentagon’s Office of the Director for Defense Research and Engineering.

This is what the sources mean by a “legacy program”: not one office surviving for eight decades, but work moving through military, intelligence, atomic and private organizations.

In their account, Kammler supplied personnel, sites, records and a model of compartmentalisation.

What The Sources Mean By “Non-Human”

Before returning to Roswell, one distinction in that chronology matters.

When these sources say “non-human”, they do not simply mean “extraterrestrial”.

One Intelligence Community source told Liberation Times that several non-primate intelligences have lived on or near Earth for longer than recorded history.

Whistleblowers speaking to Liberation Times usually use “non-human intelligence” or “advanced intelligences of unknown origin”. Liberation Times has also reported claims about rival non-human factions.

Congress has used similar language. UAP Disclosure Act language introduced by Senators Chuck Schumer and Mike Rounds, and sponsored by then-Senator Marco Rubio - now Secretary of State - referred to “unidentified anomalous phenomena, technologies of unknown origin, and non-human intelligence.”

The distinction also matters when reading official statements. At a November 2024 AARO roundtable, Director Jon Kosloski said the office had found no verifiable evidence of “extraterrestrial beings, activity or technology.”

In a June 2025 exchange published by Liberation Times, Kyle Warfel asked Pentagon spokesperson Susan Gough if that statement could be broadened to non-human or unknown intelligence. She replied: “No, you may not amend my statement.”

AARO’s FY2025 annual report used broader language, saying there is no evidence that government or private organizations captured or exploited material derived from UAP.

The sources argue that a craft already known inside a classified program would no longer be “unidentified”.

The same Intelligence Community source described “strangers”: aggressive, reptile-like beings said to be based on the Moon and in competition with the more empathetic “Nordic” group.

The source did not describe a conventional war;

“Competition between the sides may be nearly as old as humanity itself. What I've heard described isn't an outright war, but rather a scaled-down adversarial relationship. It's unclear which sides have aligned with international governments, or which sides are cooperating with factions within the program. It's quite possible that every government has had to manage this competition among the sides.”

That is the framework behind the sources’ use of “non-human”.

It also matters to how they interpret the next event in the chronology: Roswell.

Roswell As An Echo

When the chronology reaches July 1947, the sources do not treat Roswell as the beginning. They say the underlying program was already more than a decade old.

They say pilot Kenneth Arnold’s June 1947 sighting involved swept-wing craft, not discs. Roswell followed weeks later in New Mexico.

In their account, both were outward signs of the earlier Italian and German work.

More specifically, they say the Roswell incident involved two human-made machines derived from the older program: a Nazi design moved through Spain to Argentina, and a Wright Field prototype built by an Italian-American-German team using help from the Magenta vehicle. Liberation Times previously reported this allegation.

Several people with relevant backgrounds could not confirm that reconstruction. Some rejected it. It remains one of the chronology’s least secure claims.

A separate story circulated among German rocket-scientist families in Huntsville.

In Peter Santenello’s 2024 film on Paperclip, a retired Army officer identified only as “Theo” said he was the grandson of engineer Theodor Vowe.

He recalled a family story that Wernher von Braun was “immediately secreted away” to Roswell after the incident.

The Kammler Connection

Let’s return finally to the man at its center.

Kammler did not need a flying saucer to make himself valuable.

By 1945, he knew where some of the Reich’s most sensitive weapons, engineers, factories and records were hidden.

The question is whether he took that map to the grave - or into American custody.

The sources speaking to Liberation Times say there was more inside that network: an Ahnenerbe-linked exploitation effort, Magenta technology and a system of compartmentalisation that later crossed into the United States.

That larger story remains unverified.

But Kammler’s fate is not a footnote to it. It is the hinge. If he survived, the man who knew where Nazi Germany hid some of its most sensitive work may have carried that knowledge into the American system that emerged after the war.

Notes:

If this account is accurate, it would point towards a very different origin story for at least part of the modern UFO mystery.

But that does not mean every element of the story should be accepted at face value. Intelligence narratives can serve many purposes, and the possibilities range from a substantially true account, to a mixture of genuine information and later embellishment, to a counter-intelligence story designed to obscure something else entirely.

Liberation Times has taken the decision to report these claims because the sources involved are known to us and have demonstrated a credible track record in relation to information previously provided.

That history does not, by itself, verify every detail of what they now allege, but it is an important part of the editorial judgement behind publishing their account. That uncertainty should not be read as a reason to dismiss the sources behind this investigation. Rather, it reflects the difficulty of reconstructing events deliberately hidden for decades, where testimony, intelligence activity and fragmentary documentation overlap.

What remains striking is that each version of the story leads back to the same figure: Hans Kammler. Even leaving the alleged non-human technology aside, the possibility that one of the most powerful SS officials involved in the machinery of the Holocaust survived the collapse of Nazi Germany and passed into American custody would itself represent an extraordinary historical scandal.

Establishing what happened to Kammler - and what the United States believed he knew - may ultimately prove more consequential than any single claim surrounding the technology attributed to him.

item.description: Investigative journalist Tom O’Neill has described an extraordinary conversation with a senior congressional staffer who, he says, claimed classified briefings on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) included information about recovered craft, recovered beings and technology being exploited for U.S. defense purposes.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 4 September 2026

Investigative journalist Tom O’Neill has described an extraordinary conversation with a senior congressional staffer who, he says, claimed classified briefings on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) included information about recovered craft, recovered beings and technology being exploited for U.S. defense purposes.

O’Neill made the comments during an August appearance on Andrew Gold’s Heretics podcast, weeks after testifying under oath before Congress about the CIA’s MKULTRA program.

The alleged encounter occurred while O’Neill was in Washington preparing for that testimony.

On June 30, O’Neill appeared before the House Oversight Committee’s Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets at its hearing, Mind Control and Accountability: Uncovering the Truth of the CIA’s MKULTRA Project. The task force was chaired by Republican Representative Anna Paulina Luna.

Five days earlier, on June 25, O’Neill attended Disclosure Forum 2026, an all-day UAP event organized by the Disclosure Foundation in the Kennedy Caucus Room of the Russell Senate Office Building.

The event brought together lawmakers, scientists and former national-security officials to discuss UAP transparency, congressional oversight and the implications of disclosure. Participants included Senator Mike Rounds and Representatives Luna, Eric Burlison, André Carson and Suhas Subramanyam, alongside former senior congressional staffer Kirk McConnell and former Pentagon intelligence official Christopher Mellon.

O’Neill said he had not travelled to Washington because of any particular expertise on UAP, but had accepted an invitation to attend the forum before beginning preparations for his MKULTRA appearance.

During the event, O’Neill said he left to attend a private preparation meeting with Democratic minority staff ahead of the MKULTRA hearing. Because Republicans controlled the task force and had called the hearing, O’Neill said the Democratic staff wanted to know in advance what he intended to tell lawmakers.

According to O’Neill, the congressional staffer escorting him to that meeting already knew where he had been.

“You’re coming from the disclosure conference, right?” O’Neill recalled the staffer asking.

When O’Neill asked how he knew, the staffer allegedly replied: “We all work together. We know everything that’s going on.”

The conversation then turned to UAP. O’Neill told the staffer that he remained agnostic and deliberately avoided becoming immersed in the subject because of the demands of his own investigations.

The response, according to O’Neill, was shocking.

“If you knew what we knew,” the staffer allegedly told him, “you wouldn’t be agnostic.”

O’Neill said the individual explained that, as a senior congressional staffer, he accompanied the lawmaker he worked for into SCIFs - Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities - secure locations used for the discussion and review of highly classified information.

According to O’Neill, the staffer told him: “I go in, and I see what they see, and it’s terrifying.”

O’Neill then asked why government-released UAP imagery remained limited or indistinct despite growing demands for disclosure. He said the staffer responded that the government could not reveal everything because some information related directly to capabilities being developed for national defense.

O’Neill recalled the staffer saying that the United States possessed “recovered crafts and recovered beings,” and claimed knowledge obtained from recovered technology was being used to understand capabilities conventional human-made aircraft could not reproduce.

O’Neill paraphrased the argument as being that revealing detailed information about matters such as UAP velocity, propulsion or other unusual performance characteristics could expose technology being developed for U.S. military applications to adversaries.

O’Neill also described another striking detail from his meeting with the Democratic staff.

He said the same individual told him that exposure to classified information could be psychologically disturbing, claiming that congressional personnel who entered SCIFs sometimes experienced nightmares because of what they learned.

The Democratic staffers, according to O’Neill, were later present at the MKULTRA hearing itself. However, none of the task force’s five Democratic members - Ranking Member Jasmine Crockett, Stephen Lynch, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Summer Lee or Dave Min - ultimately attended.

Liberation Times previously reported in 2023 that Senate Intelligence Committee members had heard whistleblower testimony about hidden legacy UAP programs which, according to multiple sources, had been verified to some extent.

Sources also told Liberation Times in 2022 that classified UAP briefings and videos had “altered the lives of those involved.”

O’Neill’s account adds a striking new dimension to that reporting. During his interview with Gold, he said the congressional staffer told him that personnel exposed to classified information in SCIFs could suffer nightmares, and claimed that staffers with such access had been provided with psychological support to help them cope with what they had learned.

O’Neill’s account also comes amid renewed speculation that President Donald Trump could eventually go further and publicly acknowledge the existence of non-human intelligence.

The speculation follows an unprecedented White House-led UAP disclosure initiative, which has seen government records, videos and other materials released across five tranches since May.

Speaking to Sky News this week, barrister Jonathan Caplan KC, who has extensively researched the subject and developed a substantial network of sources, said:

“The debate now is no longer whether this is a real phenomenon or not - in Washington, it’s an open secret that it is. The debate now is trying to force disclosure, because Congress has been misled for 80 years…”

In his book Not for Disclosure, Caplan alleges that a small number of members of the Senate Intelligence Committee have been briefed, on a highly restricted basis, about the recovery of UAP craft. He further claims that some members of the House Intelligence Committee’s CIA Subcommittee have also been given access to the same information.
