item.title: British MP Says He Was “Definitely Misled” Over UK’s Five Eyes UFO Cooperation
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: British MP Clive Lewis has said he was “definitely misled” by the Ministry of Defence (MOD) over the United Kingdom’s cooperation with Five Eyes allies on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP).
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 29 August 2026

British MP Clive Lewis has said he was “definitely misled” by the Ministry of Defence (MOD) over the United Kingdom’s cooperation with Five Eyes allies on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP).

Lewis, the Labour MP for Norwich South and a former shadow defence secretary, is calling for greater transparency and democratic accountability over the issue.

He made the comments during a conversation with Dr Peter Skafish, co-founder and executive director of the Sol Foundation, a U.S.-based UAP research institute and policy think tank.

Skafish drew attention to questions Lewis had submitted to the MOD about whether Britain was working with the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand - its partners in the Five Eyes intelligence alliance - on UAP.

Skafish said:

“I believe one or two of your questions concerned whether the United Kingdom was working with other Five Eyes governments on the UAP issue - and, in both cases, I believe you received a negative answer.”

Lewis replied:

“Yes, that’s right. And yet we know that’s not the case. I think Five Eyes [members] have openly said they are [working together on the issue].

“So, have I been lied to? I’ve definitely been misled.”

The exchange followed a series of written parliamentary questions Lewis submitted in July and August 2025 about the MOD’s knowledge and investigation of UAP, as well as its involvement in international initiatives.

The initial questions were answered by Luke Pollard, who was then Minister for the Armed Forces and now serves as Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry.

Pollard said that the MOD had not conducted or commissioned any UAP studies since 2013. He also repeated that the department had stopped investigating sightings in 2009 after concluding that none of those reported over more than 50 years had indicated a military threat to the United Kingdom.

But it was Pollard’s answer on international cooperation that drew Lewis’s criticism.

Pollard stated:

‘The Ministry of Defence has not participated in any international groupings specifically focused on Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP) since May 2023.’

Lewis then asked whether UK cooperation with the Five Eyes UAP Caucus was ongoing.

Rather than answering yes or no, Veterans and People Minister Louise Sandher-Jones referred him back to Pollard’s earlier response.

Those answers sit uneasily alongside a documentary trail showing that British officials had been drawn into Five Eyes UAP coordination over a period of several years.

A Five Eyes Paper Trail Dating Back to 2021

That trail begins with the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force, or UAPTF, the U.S. Navy-led body established by the Pentagon in August 2020.

Its mission was to detect, analyse and catalogue UAP that could potentially threaten U.S. national security. The task force was later replaced by what would eventually be known as the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO).

In June 2025, John Greenewald of The Black Vault published U.S. Navy emails showing that an introductory briefing between the UAPTF and Five Eyes representatives was being arranged in late 2021.

Further correspondence was later released in New Zealand following an appeal under the country’s Official Information Act.

The New Zealand material was provided to Liberation Times by Australian UAP researcher Grant Lavac, who has used freedom-of-information requests to trace Five Eyes engagement with UAP and previously brought the official agenda for the May 2023 caucus into the public domain.

The email chain carried the subject line ‘UAPTF Intro (unclassified)’ and described the proposed event as an ‘Introduction for FVEYS Office to UAP Task Force.’

Initially scheduled for 30 November 2021 and later moved to 8 December, the correspondence included British officials Owen Rimmer and Annabelle Janes alongside representatives from Australia, Canada and New Zealand.

Lavac identified Rimmer as a Royal Navy lieutenant commander. Although little additional information about his career is publicly available, the correspondence shows that he acted as the principal UK coordinator for the proposed briefing, forwarding the invitation and serving as a point of contact with U.S. and Five Eyes officials.

Janes is a senior British Army officer with a background in military intelligence and international liaison.

In 2010, while holding the rank of major, she served as a UK exchange officer at the U.S. Army’s National Ground Intelligence Center in Virginia. She was subsequently identified as commanding officer of the British Army’s Land Intelligence Fusion Centre and has since been promoted to colonel. In 2025, she was serving as the British defence attaché to Thailand.

The records establish that Five Eyes officials were coordinating with the UAPTF. They do not show that the briefing took place in 2021: both the New Zealand correspondence and Greenewald’s U.S. records indicate that it was postponed.

Formal meetings were not the only sign of UAP-related intelligence circulating within Five Eyes at the time.

Liberation Times previously reported that an intelligence assessment classified an object engaged by a Royal Air Force Typhoon over Syria in 2021 as UAP.

The RAF described it as a hostile drone and said it had been destroyed. Journalists Jeremy Corbell and George Knapp, who said they had been exposed to the Five Eyes assessment, stated that it did not confirm the object’s destruction.

The assessment has not been released publicly, so those details cannot be independently verified. The episode nevertheless offers a glimpse of how UAP-related information may have circulated among allies even as the MOD maintained that it no longer investigated the subject.

From a Postponed Briefing to a Formal UAP Caucus

An email supplied to Liberation Times by Lavac confirms that a Five Eyes meeting eventually occurred in 2022.

In the email, sent to another researcher in June 2025, Pentagon spokesperson Susan Gough wrote:

‘We don’t comment on the details of meetings with our Five Eyes partners, including which members were in attendance.

‘Please note that the 2022 meeting was with AARO, not the UAPTF. AARO had replaced the UAPTF by then.’

The Pentagon did not identify the countries represented. Since AARO later called the May 2023 gathering its first Five Eyes UAP Working Group, the 2022 event appears to have been an earlier introductory meeting.

Lavac repeatedly asked whether the 2022 engagement was the UAPTF briefing postponed from late 2021, but Gough did not answer.

The UK’s participation is clearer in May 2023.

An official Pentagon agenda shows that the inaugural Five Eyes UAP Caucus Working Group was held on 24 May 2023. The United Kingdom was listed alongside Australia, Canada and New Zealand as one of the partners scheduled to provide a UAP update.

The agenda also looked ahead to possible reporting networks, shared databases, collection planning and further meetings.

As previously reported by Liberation Times, the MOD’s Defence Intelligence Secretariat later confirmed that two of its officials attended. An Information Commissioner’s Office decision also records that confirmation.

The Pentagon subsequently indicated that the discussions continued.

In June 2024, Gough told Liberation Times that AARO ‘continues to discuss areas of mutual interest and concern related to UAP with its FVEY partners.’

Gough did not say whether every Five Eyes country took part in every later discussion. But the MOD’s refusal to answer Lewis’s follow-up leaves Britain’s position unclear.

After the names of Rimmer and Janes emerged, Lavac requested their UAP and Five Eyes-related correspondence from the MOD.

In a response dated 31 July 2025, the MOD refused to confirm or deny whether it held relevant records, citing national security, defence, security bodies and international relations.

The MOD stressed that its refusal did not prove the records existed, although it referred to Britain’s work with international partners on ‘collaborative joint defence matters.’

The evidence requires a careful distinction. The 2021 and 2022 material does not directly contradict Pollard’s answer, which concerned participation after May 2023. Nor does the Pentagon’s 2024 statement establish that Britain took part in every subsequent discussion.

What the record does show is that British officials were involved before and during the May 2023 caucus, that AARO later described discussions with Five Eyes partners as continuing, and that the MOD declined to say whether the United Kingdom remained involved.

Australia’s Contradictory Account

The transparency questions raised by Lewis are not confined to Britain. Australia has faced its own contradictions over the same May 2023 meeting.

On 19 July 2023, the Australian Department of Defence responded to a Question on Notice from then Greens senator Peter Whish-Wilson by categorically denying that Australia had attended AARO’s UAP briefing in May 2023.

The denial was clear and unambiguous. Yet on 15 December 2023, less than six months later, the department reversed its position and acknowledged that a defence representative from the Australian Embassy in Washington, D.C., had attended the inaugural AARO Five Eyes UAP Caucus Working Group briefing.

It also confirmed that Australia had not merely observed the meeting, but had actively presented at it.

The inconsistency followed an earlier exchange over UAP discussions with the United States.

On 17 May 2022, during the first U.S. congressional hearing on UAP in more than half a century, Deputy Director of Naval Intelligence Scott Bray testified that the Pentagon had brought allies and international partners into its discussions.

Six months later, on 9 November 2022, Senator Whish-Wilson questioned then Chief of Air Force Air Marshal Robert Chipman during Senate Estimates.

In light of Australia’s close defence relationship with the United States, the senator asked whether Australian intelligence or the Air Force had participated in those discussions.

Chipman said he was not aware of any formal discussions with the United States and that such matters would have crossed his desk if they had occurred.

Yet Australian officials had already been included in preparations for the late-2021 Five Eyes briefing, although the records indicate that it was postponed. The Pentagon has also confirmed that a Five Eyes meeting was held with AARO in 2022, but has not identified the countries represented.

Lavac told Liberation Times that the lack of transparency was "very concerning".

Lavac added:

"The Chief of Air Force leads all discussions on UAP in Australia when called before a Senate estimates, so if there's one person that needs to know what is happening on the UAP topic in an Australian context and our discussions with allies, it's him."

"He was either completely uninformed due to a complete lack of intelligence sharing, or there's a high-degree of incompetence, or it's something more sinister like plausible deniability or deliberate obfuscation. Any one of those scenarios are of great concern. What confidence can Australian taxpayers have that their elected representatives are going to have their pertinent questions answered truthfully and accurately by those in positions of authority in the Australian Department of Defence?"

Against that wider Five Eyes backdrop, Lewis is seeking to bring the unresolved question of Britain’s involvement under closer scrutiny in the House of Commons.

“We’re a Democracy Too”

Although UFOs and UAP have periodically surfaced in Parliament, some of the most prominent interventions have come from the House of Lords, including a dedicated debate in 1979 and an exchange initiated by Lord Sarfraz in 2021. Sustained engagement from elected MPs remains rare.

Lewis is therefore a notable exception, particularly given his experience as a former shadow defence secretary and a British Army infantry officer who served in Afghanistan.

However, Lewis is cautious about what UAP may represent and does not assert that they are of non-human origin.

Lewis said:

“I don’t make a public judgement on whether UAP are real, whether the technology exists or whether we have been visited by non-human intelligence.

“I just think there is a discrepancy in what we’re being told, and I think the British public have a right to know.

“The U.S. public seem to be hearing things that we should also be hearing here in the United Kingdom. We’re a democracy too.”

He added:

“The approach I take in the United Kingdom is that, whether UAP exist or not, you can already see from what’s coming out in the United States that there are contradictions which need to be dealt with.

“At some point, someone somewhere in my government, or one of the institutions around it, has decided that the British public should not hear about this. As a parliamentarian, I have an issue with that.

“I accept there are some things which are classified for good reason that I don’t need to know about.

“But when we look back through history, there are many things governments did not need to hide. They were concealed not because of the security of the realm, but because they represented inconvenient truths.”

For Lewis, the unresolved question is not what UAP ultimately represent, but whether the government has given Parliament and the British public a candid account of the country’s involvement.

item.title: The Push for UFO Disclosure Intensifies as Pressure Mounts on Donald Trump
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: A growing number of advocates are pressing President Trump to reveal what they believe is evidence of advanced non‑human intelligence and its technologies interacting with humanity, an effort that has accelerated in recent days.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 19 August 2026

A growing number of advocates are pressing President Trump to reveal what they believe is evidence of advanced non‑human intelligence and its technologies interacting with humanity, an effort that has accelerated in recent days. 

The push follows new remarks from Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) whistleblower and former U.S. Air Force intelligence officer David Grusch, who appeared last week on the Dr Phil podcast, urging the Trump administration to take decisive action on the UAP issue.

Grusch’s comments come as Stephen Miller, one of Trump’s closest and longest‑serving advisers, has reportedly been asked by the President to examine the UAP portfolio.

Miller, a central architect of Trump‑era policy and a dominant voice within his political operation, is now seen by disclosure advocates as a key figure in determining how the administration approaches the subject.

During the interview with Dr Phil - a friend of President Trump - Grusch said, “I hope President Trump delivers on his promise – I think this is going to be the singular thing which is going to define his legacy.”

He went on to argue that the responsibility now rests with Trump’s inner circle, adding, “Mr Miller and the President’s team need to realise this is going to be the defining moment of his legacy, because even if Trump doesn’t disclose, the genie is out of the bottle now and we’re going to look back on ‘what did the President know and why didn’t he get the information out?’”

Since 14 August, documentary filmmaker James Fox has released a series of four videos featuring different UAP whistleblowers - including David Grusch - urging President Trump to take action on the issue. 

Their appeals focus on the declassification of UAP‑related material - including photographs and documentation of retrieved craft and alleged non‑human bodies - and on securing immunity and protection for individuals who could face repercussions for violating Non‑Disclosure Agreements to share what they know.

The additional whistleblowers appearing in Fox’s videos include Dylan Borland, a former Air Force geospatial intelligence specialist; Matthew Brown, a former Department of War official; and Dr Eric Davis, an aerospace engineer known for his work on advanced propulsion concepts.

Grusch, in his appeal to President Trump, said he is prepared to “provide a full historical accounting to the National Security Council principals, the White House Chief of Staff and make any supporting public statements that are authorised to help this administration move disclosure forward.”

He added that he is ready to assist the administration in identifying the records, programs and personnel involved in classified UAP activities, and in bringing “any improperly concealed activities back under lawful presidential and congressional oversight.”

He concluded his message with a direct call to action: “Mr President, give us the authorisation, and we’re ready to go.”

Another disclosure effort is emerging from billionaire and Trump donor Robert Bigelow, whose interest in UAPs spans several decades. Two weeks ago, Bigelow said that in February he advised President Trump on how he might address the nation regarding the issue.

“I was emphasizing that the disclosure process, starting with confirmation, is a big deal. That, you know, it really is important for somebody like the President of the United States to say, ‘yeah, they’re real, they’re here. And eliminate all the other nonsense, all the noise that’s been going on for 80 years,’” Bigelow said.

Describing the guidance he offered, Bigelow stated:

“This, this is what I want you to say, Mr President: ‘A non-human, intelligent presence has been on Earth for a very long time, using spacecraft and with performances completely beyond our capabilities and our human physics.’ And that’s it, to say nothing else. That’s it, that’s all. Because what this is, is disclosure. And it’s actually confirmation.”

Bigelow has recently launched a new podcast series with veteran investigative journalist George Knapp, and in the latest episode he appeared to take a more cautious stance on disclosure than Grusch, emphasising the need to protect secrecy.

In yesterday’s podcast episode, discussing the private‑sector gatekeepers allegedly involved in reverse‑engineering programs related to non‑human technology, Bigelow said:

“The companies need more money. They need more scientists involved, but they have to maintain their secrecy at all costs because we are in competition with China and Russia on the exact same thing [non-human technology], and they don't have the concerns about secrecy that we do.”

Outlining his view of how disclosure should unfold, Bigelow added:

“It needs to be a process, a step-by-step, partial process delivery. It needs to be truthful, and we need to engage, find ways to engage one of the most important assets that this country has - it’s the gatekeepers- and do it in a way that is really a great new era of partnership that has never existed for 80 years.”

Liberation Times understands that advocates are attempting to persuade President Trump to deliver some form of disclosure speech before the midterm elections on 3 November 2026. 

Their goal is to prompt a public acknowledgement that some UAPs are of non-human origin.  

Lue Elizondo, the former head of the Pentagon’s UAP program AATIP, is also widely believed to be in a position to work with the Trump administration and help guide a potential disclosure effort.

Sources also tell Liberation Times that the U.S. government - including its UAP office, the All‑domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) -  is aware of data indicating extreme‑performance incidents. 

These reportedly include objects traversing the Atlantic Ocean from end to end in three seconds, as well as similar episodes of rapid acceleration observed in the vicinity of Japan.

Another source told Liberation Times that the CIA’s chief scientist acts as an operational gatekeeper for programs involving the retrieval and reverse-engineering of vehicles allegedly of non-human origin within the Agency’s Directorate of Science and Technology. According to the source, the CIA’s deputy director within the Science and Technology directorate serves as the administrative gatekeeper for those programs.

Betty Sapp, former Director of the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), has been described by Liberation Times sources as another key gatekeeper. According to those sources, Sapp worked with former Director of National Intelligence James Clapper and his deputy Stephanie O’Sullivan on an Obama‑era program focused on locating UAP, recovering them, and attempting to reverse‑engineer their technology.

In his autobiography - ‘Facts and Fears’ - Clapper highlighted Sapp and O’Sullivan as women who consistently outperformed their male colleagues.

Sapp had previously worked with Clapper in the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence or USD(I), and he later helped advance her career by supporting her appointment as the NRO’s deputy director in April 2009.

Clapper writes, ‘when the NRO director retired in April, we moved Betty Sapp, my USD(I) deputy for portfolio, programs, and resources, to NRO as the principal deputy director.’

Since appearing in the UAP documentary Age of Disclosure, Liberation Times understands that Clapper has stepped back from efforts to promote UAP transparency. One source told Liberation Times that he has grown uncomfortable with the recent surge of attention.

Some sources told Liberation Times they fear that whistleblowers could face retaliation if the UAP issue slips from the political agenda. 

Whether President Trump is prepared to disclose any information related to UAPs remains unclear, with sources offering differing accounts of his level of interest and of how the White House is currently approaching the issue.

item.title: Intelligence Watchdog Warns of FBI Referral Over Alleged Disclosure of UAP Whistleblower Testimony
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: The Office of the Intelligence Community Inspector General (ICIG) has provided a statement to Liberation Times in response to allegations that details of testimony given by an Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) whistleblower were disclosed to a journalist.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 11 August 2026

The Office of the Intelligence Community Inspector General (ICIG) has provided a statement to Liberation Times in response to allegations that details of testimony given by an Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) whistleblower were disclosed to a journalist. 

Investigative journalist Jeremy Corbell has alleged that an ODNI source disclosed details of testimony provided by Dylan Borland, a UAP whistleblower who has made protected disclosures to the IC OIG and Congress. According to Corbell, the information included claims concerning an alleged UAP program codenamed ‘Rubik’s Cube’.

Speaking to Liberation Times, Borland corroborated the allegation that classified whistleblower testimony was intentionally disclosed to Corbell.

Borland is a former U.S. Air Force geospatial intelligence specialist who later worked as a senior analyst for defence contractors BAE Systems and Intrepid Solutions, examining video, radar and advanced electro-optical imagery. 

In sworn testimony before Congress in September 2025, he identified himself as a federal whistleblower who had provided information to both the Intelligence Community Office of the Inspector General (IC OIG) and the Pentagon’s All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) concerning alleged craft, technologies and legacy UAP programs operating without congressional oversight.

A spokesperson for the Office of the Intelligence Community Inspector General responded to the allegation with a carefully worded statement. While declining to confirm whether Borland had provided testimony or whether any investigation was underway, the office emphasised that it is legally required to protect confidential whistleblowers and information that could reveal their identities. 

The spokesperson also warned that any unauthorised disclosure of protected information could result in removal from federal service and referral to the FBI or another investigative authority:

‘We are aware of a recent public claim by a journalist concerning testimony allegedly provided to IC OIG.  Subject to limited exceptions, IC OIG is required by law to protect from public disclosure the identity of confidential whistleblowers and certain information that could reasonably be expected to reveal their identities.  IC OIG takes these obligations seriously.

‘Consistent with longstanding policy and practice, IC OIG can neither confirm nor deny the existence of any pending or ongoing investigation.  Any unauthorized disclosure of information protected by law, including information that identifies of could reasonably be expected to identify a confidential whistleblower, may constitute grounds for removal from Federal service and may also warrant referral to FBI or other appropriate investigative authorities.’

Corbell’s allegation concerning Borland forms part of a broader controversy surrounding ODNI’s Director’s Initiatives Group (DIG).

Corbell also alleges that the same unnamed ODNI official circulated damaging claims said to have emerged from another whistleblower’s private meeting with the group.

As Liberation Times previously reported, the group conducted its own inquiry into UAP-related allegations and met privately with whistleblower Matthew Brown at the Liberty Crossing Intelligence Campus in Virginia. Brown said he had been approached by the individual leading the effort and invited to provide information about his experiences.

According to Brown, the group did not appear focused on the substance of what he was saying. 

Instead, he felt they were more interested in learning which classified compartments and sub-compartments he had accessed.

This left him with the impression that they wanted to work out how he knew what he knew and stop similar disclosures from happening again.

Brown believes this led to him being wrongly labelled antisemitic.

Brown denied those claims and believed they formed part of an attempt to discredit him. Borland was also named among the UAP whistleblowers allegedly subjected to intimidation or smear efforts connected to the inquiry.

Asked about that specific allegation, an ODNI spokesperson provided the following statement to Liberation Times:

‘ODNI has been and continues to be focused on carrying out the objectives of President Trump's executive orders and mandates, including assisting with any relevant information related to UAPs.’  

The statement did not directly address whether information from Brown’s meeting had been disclosed or whether ODNI was examining the allegation.

ODNI also sought to distinguish the secure setting of the meeting from the legal protections attached to it.

It noted that information discussed inside a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) is not automatically classified, since unclassified matters may also be discussed there, and stressed that simply speaking inside a SCIF does not in itself confer whistleblower protections.

Separate from the alleged disclosures, questions have also arisen about the investigative approach adopted within the DIG, which was established under former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard.

Multiple sources who have spoken to Liberation Times claim that the investigation was compromised by elements linked to the CIA, allegedly to discourage Congress from pursuing further UAP hearings and legislation, while deterring additional whistleblowers from coming forward publicly.

James E. Erdman III, a senior CIA operations officer assigned to ODNI on a joint-duty posting, was among the earliest members of the DIG and led its work on UAP, anomalous health incidents and the origins of COVID-19. 

Erdman subsequently alleged that the CIA obstructed the group’s work, monitored its communications and tracked its contacts with whistleblowers. In testimony provided to the Senate in May this year, he described himself as a senior CIA operations officer and alleged that the agency had investigated DIG members and monitored their computer and telephone activity.

However, Erdman’s own recent public comments about UAP claims and the wider UFO community have raised questions about the assumptions informing the group’s inquiry. 

Those concerns are particularly relevant because Erdman, as a CIA officer assigned to ODNI, led the examination of allegations that implicated his home agency in a secretive UAP retrieval and reverse-engineering effort.

Writing on X in response to comments by journalist Walter Kirn, Erdman stated:

‘I generally lean in on believing fighter pilots and submariners with everything to lose when they choose to risk vocalizing their experiences to their chain of command. I just don’t think we can draw a straight line between all their stories and alien life just yet and they don't always jump to that conclusion either. They want answers just as much as the next guy.

‘There is also … a whole lot of grifting and lies infecting the UFO community. If anyone is up to the task of discerning between fact and fiction, I have no doubt @walterkirn is the guy. Nothing has been black and white on this issue. Videos released without explanation, often released during unfavorable news cycles, and trumpeted by the same set of inter-connected alien-chasers should not be propagated as evidence.

‘COVID also taught us how to identify PsyOps… We shouldn’t forget hard fought lessons.

‘If the government doesn’t provide first hand evidence of biologics, evidence of a crash retrieval program, or any object that is the subject of an ongoing reverse engineering program … treat it as a known unknown, a lie, a mistake, or a grift until proven otherwise.’

Erdman appeared willing to credit military witnesses describing incidents outside the secrecy of alleged UAP Special Access Programs and Controlled Access Programs.

By contrast, he characterised claims involving non-human biologics, recovered craft and reverse-engineering efforts - allegedly concealed within those compartments - as lies, mistakes or grifts unless direct evidence was produced.

That position raises questions about the approach taken during the UAP investigations Erdman led within the DIG and the treatment of whistleblowers.

Requiring publicly available proof from programs alleged to have been deliberately hidden behind the highest levels of classification risks prejudging the very claims the group was tasked with examining.

The concern is heightened by accounts from whistleblowers who interacted with the DIG. They claim that, rather than receiving an impartial hearing, they faced suspicion, intimidation and attempts to undermine their credibility.

Erdman’s remarks do not establish that he personally participated in such conduct. However, their adversarial framing raises questions about whether allegations concerning covert UAP programs were investigated with sufficient independence and an open mind.

Concerns about the DIG’s work form part of wider allegations concerning resistance to UAP disclosure within ODNI.

Three sources have told Liberation Times that figures within ODNI linked to the CIA are resisting efforts by the Trump administration to release more substantial information concerning UAP.

Those sources identified Aaron Lukas, the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, as one of the officials allegedly providing such resistance.

Lukas previously spent more than two decades within the Intelligence Community and served as a CIA Chief of Station. According to his official ODNI biography, he managed sensitive clandestine programs, conducted covert operations and maintained liaison relationships around the world.

Liberation Times has not independently substantiated the allegations concerning Lukas.

item.title: UFO History Is Being Shaped in Washington - No One Knows How This Ends
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description:
No one knows how this will end.
It could become one of the most consequential moments in human history. Or, ten years from now, it may be little more than a fascinating story in a White House memoir - a glimpse of what might have been.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 3 August 2026

No one knows how this will end.

It could become one of the most consequential moments in human history. Or, ten years from now, it may be little more than a fascinating story in a White House memoir - a glimpse of what might have been.

Last month, Liberation Times reported, citing multiple sources, that a presidential speech confirming that some UFOs - officially described as Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) - are of non-human origin had been prepared.

Liberation Times understands that the speech is now under consideration. It could be delivered before this November’s midterm elections. If it is not delivered by then, any plans could be abandoned.

The scale and gravity of what is unfolding have received remarkably little attention.

White House Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy Stephen Miller is reportedly leading the administration’s work on UAP.

Meanwhile, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence has confirmed the creation of an Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Governance Board.

The interagency board brings together the military, law enforcement, the intelligence community and civilian agencies. 

It is intended to coordinate investigations, improve the collection and analysis of information and assist with the ongoing UAP declassification process, which commenced in May 2026 following a directive from President Trump.

The Office of the Director of National Intelligence has also confirmed that several groups of outside experts are advising the board.

Yet only one of those groups and its members has been publicly identified: the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Science Advisory Council.

The purpose, expertise and membership of the other advisory groups remain unknown. Those involved have not publicly revealed their roles.

Together, these developments point to an organised effort spanning the White House, the United States intelligence community and several fields of outside expertise.

Then, on Saturday 1 August, came perhaps the clearest indication yet that the White House is serious.

Representative Eric Burlison released a memorandum that the Trump administration had authorised his office to make public.

Signed the previous day by Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence Aaron Lukas, it implements President Trump’s direction to release current and former government employees and contractors from nondisclosure agreements, oaths and other commitments when reporting information about UAP to authorised officials.

It also directs that such information be provided to the newly created presidential task force - the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters - for review and potential declassification.

The memorandum was distributed to 18 senior intelligence, law-enforcement and military officials. Intelligence agencies have 30 days to appoint designated representatives and inform their workforces of the President’s order.

Its most extraordinary language goes further. It states that any prior or existing nondisclosure agreement that prevents information from being reported to the President or his designated representatives is no longer in force.

It must be noted that the memorandum provides no immunity or protection for those threatened or punished for violating NDAs.

However, these steps provide perhaps the clearest evidence yet that Trump is seriously contemplating further disclosure.

Liberation Times understands that advocates are now competing to shape what form any disclosure would take should the President decide to proceed. Sources familiar with the current effort say some private defence contractors and individuals with ties to the CIA are resisting broader disclosure.

Others involved in current efforts - from participants in White House discussions to members of the unidentified advisory groups - have remained silent. 

One notable exception is television personality Dr Phil McGraw, a personal friend of the President.

In the latest episode of his podcast, released on 30 July, McGraw asked listeners to imagine the government standing at a podium and declaring: “We are not alone.”

He described such a declaration as potentially the biggest news in human history. He also warned that releasing the information without preparation or context could allow fear, rumour and exploitation to fill the void.

Taken alone, this might be dismissed as a dramatic thought experiment.

But McGraw later made several far more consequential statements.

He said he is engaged in an active dialogue with President Trump and the administration about the issue. 

He also said he had advised the White House that any disclosure would require careful pacing and preparation.

McGraw then stated plainly: “I know President Trump is serious about this.”

His own sense of urgency became even clearer when the conversation turned to mental-health preparedness.

Speaking with clinical psychologist Dr Jennice Vilhauer, McGraw argued that an emergency response could not be constructed from scratch after an announcement.

“This is upon us. It is happening right now,” McGraw said.

At points, his language conveyed a striking sense of personal urgency.

McGraw described Dr John Whyte, chief executive and executive vice president of the American Medical Association, as a dear friend.

He then said he felt personally compelled to have a heart-to-heart conversation with Whyte about how the organisation’s existing infrastructure could help prepare for the consequences of disclosure.

McGraw does not appear to be treating the subject as entertainment. He appears to believe that something could happen - and that preparations should begin now.

Yet, at the time of writing on Sunday 2 August, his podcast episode had received just 69,317 views on YouTube.

That limited reach reflects a striking disconnect: while potentially historic machinery is being assembled in Washington, much of the public remains unaware of it.

Taken together, the developments are difficult to dismiss:

  • Since May 2026, the U.S. government has released four tranches of UAP records under a directive issued by President Trump

  • A presidential speech has allegedly been prepared

  • A senior White House official is reportedly directing the administration’s work

  • An interagency Governance Board has been established

  • Several groups of outside experts are advising it, although the identities and work of most remain concealed

  • A presidential task force is collecting government records and considering them for declassification

  • Government personnel are being released from nondisclosure agreements so they can report what they know - even where those agreements previously prevented information from reaching the President

  • And a personal friend of Donald Trump says he is discussing disclosure with the administration while considering how America’s medical and psychological institutions might be mobilised.

Whether this becomes a historic turning point or eventually fades into a White House memoir remains unknown. 

Either way, current events deserve far greater scrutiny from the public and the press.

item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description:
On the brink - or facing another false dawn. It’s difficult to tell.
Liberation Times understands from multiple sources that a presidential speech confirming that some UFOs are of non-human origin has been prepared.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 21 July 2026

On the brink - or facing another false dawn.

It’s difficult to tell. 

Liberation Times understands from multiple sources that a presidential speech confirming that some UFOs are of non-human origin has been prepared.

Whether President Donald Trump ever delivers it is anyone’s guess.

Presidential teams have long prepared contingency speeches and statements for events that may never occur. The existence of a draft therefore does not, by itself, mean that a final decision has been taken to deliver it. 

Trump is understood to have little personal interest in the subject. 

But this is a president deeply preoccupied with greatness and his place in history - whether through having a road named in his honour or seeking to bring Greenland under US control. 

Faced with an opportunity to define his presidency and secure an unparalleled legacy, ego may ultimately outweigh indifference. 

Liberation Times understands that several UAP disclosure advocates, some operating independently of one another, are lobbying the Trump White House to go beyond the measures announced so far. 

So far, the White House’s disclosure plan appears to mirror one developed by retired Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet, who served as acting administrator of NOAA during Trump’s first presidency.

In early 2025, he met with officials from the Trump Administration to discuss a comprehensive, whole-of-government approach to UFOs, otherwise known as Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) 

Gallaudet had previously gone on record to outline his plan for UAP disclosure. 

  • A White House-directed policy issued through an executive order or presidential memorandum

  • The establishment of an interagency group, chaired by a senior White House official or Cabinet member, to coordinate a strategy and lead efforts

  • Legislation passed in Congress aligned with White House policy, ensuring coordination between the executive branch and interagency efforts.

The first two elements of Gallaudet’s plan now appear to have materialised, at least in substance. 

Trump directed agencies to begin identifying and releasing UAP-related records, while an interagency UAP Governance Board - supported by a new Science Advisory Council - has been created to coordinate the administration’s efforts. 

The third element may now be taking shape in Congress. 

The House is expected to consider a proposal from Congressman Eric Burlison that would create an independent review board with the authority to search across government for UAP records and determine what should be released publicly.

It would also empower the federal government to take possession - while providing compensation - of any technology of unknown origin or biological evidence of non-human intelligence held by private companies or individuals. 

A broadly similar proposal has been introduced in the Senate, although neither measure has yet passed and their final form remains uncertain.

But events could yet overtake the congressional process if Trump chooses to act before any legislation is enacted. 

According to Fox News, Trump has directed agencies to waive previous nondisclosure agreements for former government employees and contractors who share UAP information through authorised government channels.

Lue Elizondo, the former head of the Pentagon’s Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, has argued that those involved in alleged legacy programs may require amnesty, immunity and even witness protection.

It is not yet clear whether Trump’s directive provides broader protections such as amnesty or immunity.

Although it does not authorise public disclosure, it creates a formal route for insiders to approach investigators - meaning one of the conditions considered essential for accelerating disclosure may now be falling into place.

By allowing officials to test claims from purported firsthand witnesses, the process could give Trump greater confidence in the evidence before deciding whether to deliver the disclosure speech understood to have been prepared.

Within the White House, Trump’s powerful deputy chief of staff, Stephen Miller, has emerged as a central figure in the effort. Congressman Burlison has described the administration, working through Miller, as “aggressively pursuing” UAP disclosure.

Given Trump’s preoccupation with legacy - and his inherent unpredictability - he may yet choose to deliver the speech prepared for him. 

If he does, the announcement itself would be only the beginning. The White House would then face the far more delicate task of helping the public understand and absorb its implications.

One figure who could assist in that effort is television psychologist Phil McGraw, better known as Dr Phil. As a familiar broadcaster and prominent Trump ally, McGraw could provide the administration with a recognisable mainstream voice through which to explore the psychological and societal consequences of disclosure.

His team was recently given an early look at the fourth tranche in the administration’s continuing release of previously secret government UAP records. According to the Need to Know podcast, McGraw told Christopher Mellon and Bryce Zabel that the material arrived with a handwritten message from Trump: “Have fun with this.” 

McGraw may not be the only outside figure being considered as part of any effort to prepare the public. NewsNation journalist Ross Coulthart has reported, citing people inside the administration, that the White House is consulting spiritual leaders and seeking advice on how the public might absorb confirmation that humanity is not alone. No participating religious leaders have been publicly identified, and the White House has not confirmed that such discussions are taking place. 

There is also speculation that former Pentagon UAP investigator Lue Elizondo could be appointed to a senior White House role overseeing the issue. 

Elizondo previously proposed the creation of an emerging-technologies ‘czar’ within the National Security Council, who would advise the President, coordinate policy across government and engage with Congress, the media and the American public. 

If appointed, Elizondo could therefore play a central role in guiding both the government’s response and the wider disclosure process.

Whether it culminates in the speech Liberation Times understands has been prepared remains anyone’s guess.

But the machinery of disclosure is now taking shape across the White House, federal agencies and Congress.

It may yet unravel. Or it may be approaching the point at which demands for a definitive answer become impossible to contain.

item.title: U.S. Conducted Successful UFO “Luring Operation,” Advocate Claims, as Government Files Detail Orb Encounters
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sharp
item.description: A UFO advocacy figure has claimed that the Office of the Director of National Intelligence conducted a successful operation designed to attract unidentified objects over a sensitive U.S. government testing facility. Jordan Flowers, executive director of the Disclosure Foundation, made the claim during an appearance on CBS News.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 12 July 2026

A UFO advocacy figure has claimed that the Office of the Director of National Intelligence conducted a successful operation designed to attract unidentified objects over a sensitive U.S. government testing facility.

Jordan Flowers, executive director of the Disclosure Foundation, made the claim during an appearance on CBS News.

The Disclosure Foundation is an advocacy group focused on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena, or UAP.

Flowers said the incident could be understood by bringing together recently released government documents and statements made publicly by members of Congress.

He said:

“When we combine that information and synthesise it with some of the comments members of Congress are making about the classified briefings they are receiving, we end up reaching some astounding conclusions based solely on information that is publicly available.

“For instance, during the December 2025 incursion in the southwestern United States over a sensitive military facility, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence was conducting a UAP-luring operation. That operation was wildly successful.

“It produced FLIR [forward-looking infrared] video and photographs of the orbs encountered as part of the operation. It resulted in an FBI 302 interview, as well as a personal statement from a senior intelligence official at ODNI, and precipitated a classified briefing for members of Congress, including [House Majority Leader Steve] Scalise and Representatives [Eric] Burlison and [Tim] Burchett.

“This event was described as incontrovertible proof that there is a real phenomenon here and as a core reason why transparency efforts have accelerated over the past few months.

“What is really interesting is that, when you synthesise that with Congressman Burlison’s public comments and the information provided, it suggests not only that AARO—the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office—and ODNI know this is a real phenomenon, but that they already have the technology and methods, with a proven track record, to lure and attract these things.

“So, suffice it to say, we need to synthesise what members of Congress are saying in addition to the data releases here. When you do that, you are able to reach some astounding conclusions using publicly available information.”

The event described by Flowers appears to be the same incident recorded in two government documents released under President Trump’s UAP disclosure initiative.

One was released in the first tranche of files and the other in the second.

  • The first document, titled USPER Statement about UAP Sighting, is described by the Department of War as an FBI 302 interview with a senior U.S. intelligence official who witnessed the encounter. An FBI 302 is the written record agents produce after interviewing a witness.

  • The second document, titled ODNI-UAP-D001, USPER Narrative, Senior USIC Official, was released in the second tranche. The Department of War describes it as a firsthand account written by a currently serving senior U.S. intelligence official who witnessed the encounters. The official was a passenger in the helicopter and described seeing glowing orbs both at close range and in the distance while a government team investigated unusual noises and UAP sightings in and around a sensitive military facility.

Together, the documents describe a series of encounters at a sensitive government testing site in the western United States in late 2025.

Although Flowers placed the event in the southwestern United States and said it occurred in December, the released records do not give the exact date or location.

The name of the facility, nearby towns, mountain range and coordinates remain hidden.

A Search for Orbs

According to the Department of War, the senior intelligence official was a passenger in a helicopter that left a Joint Operations Center with another official and two pilots.

The team was investigating unusual noises and reports of glowing orbs in and around the military facility. The objects had reportedly been seen over several previous nights, while personnel had also heard loud thuds in the surrounding mountains.

This led the crew to search for debris or other objects that might explain the sightings.

The helicopter flew low through the mountain range for several hours.

The crew examined several pieces of debris, but each was found to be part of old rockets or other projectiles left behind by years of weapons testing.

During the search, they also discovered a large cave entrance with no visible end.

There was nowhere safe to land, so the pilot circled the area before the crew recorded its location and continued the mission.

After dropping off one member of the team and refuelling, the helicopter was directed towards another area where ground personnel believed they had spotted debris.

By then, it was dark.

The pilots used night-vision goggles and the helicopter’s infrared camera, while the intelligence official watched with the naked eye.

The initial search found nothing.

As the helicopter began returning to base, however, the Joint Operations Center reported fresh detections in an area where UAP had previously been seen.

The intelligence official wrote:

‘What followed was a series of close UAP encounters lasting over an hour.’

A Super-Hot Orb

Ground observers using infrared equipment reported seeing a ‘super-hot’ orb hovering close to the ground.

It then moved away at high speed and appeared to split into two objects, which accelerated off in different directions.

According to the Department of War’s summary of the FBI interview, the orb travelled for around 20 miles and moved too quickly for the helicopter to keep up.

The ground team then reported that the object had risen from the ground and came within approximately ten feet of the helicopter.

The pilots saw the object through night-vision goggles.

They also reported seeing something smaller emerge from the two objects before travelling away in a different direction at high speed.

The helicopter attempted to follow but could not match its speed.

Swarms of Lights

The Joint Operations Center then told the crew that five military aircraft were flying in the area as part of a training mission.

The intelligence official described them as fighter jets.

A short time later, the helicopter crew saw what the official described as countless orange lights moving in different directions against the mountains.

The display lasted several minutes before fading.

The helicopter was then directed towards further detections and hovered around 700 feet above the ground.

Two large orbs appeared close to the helicopter, just above the rotor blades.

The intelligence official described them as oval-shaped and orange, with white or yellow centres.

He said they appeared to remain still while shining light in every direction.

More orbs then appeared underneath the original pair.

The official wrote:

‘After a few seconds, a third orb flared up below the pair, followed by a fourth below that, forming a total of four or five in a ‘T’ formation under the original two.’

The objects remained visible for around 10 to 15 seconds before fading in reverse order.

The pilots briefly considered landing because the objects were so close, but instead remained in the air.

Similar formations were then seen above the military aircraft.

According to the official, the orbs appeared one by one in a horizontal line and seemed to match the aircraft’s speed and direction.

They then faded and disappeared.

This happened several times as the military aircraft moved through the area and later descended to land.

The intelligence official said it appeared as though the orbs were ‘chasing’ the aircraft.

The other government record similarly states:

‘The orbs appeared to break off from [the helicopter] and pursue the [military aircraft].’

The documents describe more sightings over the next half-hour, including swarms of lights, horizontal formations and three orbs arranged in a triangle.

After returning to the Joint Operations Center, the intelligence official wrote:

‘We were virtually speechless after these observations.’

Photographs From the Same Encounters

The Department of War lists 24 images under the ‘Related Media’ section alongside the government records. Six of those images are reproduced further below.

The Department of War directly connects the images to the same exercise described by the senior intelligence official.

Its description states that the official’s account is accompanied by infrared imagery taken during the exercise by other federal personnel observing from the ground.

The images were originally released on 8 May 2026, as part of the first tranche of files published under President Trump’s UAP disclosure initiative.

A separate description on the Department of War website says:

‘The photos of UAP underneath the helicopter are from this same set of observations, taken through night vision devices by ground-based personnel.’

The black-and-white images show dark, circular objects that the Department of War says were photographed beneath the helicopter by personnel on the ground.

The government says the people operating the equipment could not identify what the objects were.

The images were provided to the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office by the FBI.

Some details were removed to protect the identities of witnesses, the location of the facility and other sensitive information unrelated to UAP.

The Department of War says nothing was removed that would alter what the images show about the objects themselves.

The documents also state that the helicopter pilots were recording during the encounter.

The Redacted ‘Successful Test’

The documents do not openly describe the mission as an attempt to lure or attract UAP.

However, the previously classified operational record contains one potentially important detail.

It says that, earlier that day, a government office had completed a ‘successful test’ at the same facility.

The name of the office and the type of test are redacted.

The Department of War also describes the encounters as taking place during an ‘exercise,’ but does not explain what the exercise involved.

The released documents therefore support some of Flowers’ claims.

They confirm that the event led to an FBI interview with a senior intelligence official.

They confirm that photographs were taken during the same series of encounters.

They also confirm that several government witnesses and sensors observed the objects.

Burlison: “This Is When the Whole Conversation Changed”

Flowers’ account closely matches comments made by Republican Representative Eric Burlison during an interview with Annie Frey two months earlier.

Burlison said:

“I was briefed on an event that occurred where they basically tried to set up a perfect-case scenario that would cause UAP to come in, and then to capture them—or to try to document or record them.

“And it was very successful. This only happened a few months ago, and this is when the whole conversation changed, because that event was one that no one could deny.”

Burlison continued:

“There were so many people who witnessed these things, and they were all credible people working in our top intelligence sector.

“They brought me in to brief me on this within a few days or weeks after the event happened. I felt that was nice that they did that; they knew I was researching this topic.”

He added:

“That briefing is the one everybody wants.

“Yes, other members of Congress have heard about this. Leader Scalise got the briefing along with a couple of other members.

“I had only told Leader Scalise about this, and now everybody wants this briefing.”

Scalise Confirms “Eye-Opening” Briefing

Burlison’s claim that House Majority Leader Steve Scalise received a briefing was later supported by Scalise himself.

However, Scalise did not publicly confirm that the briefing concerned the same incident.

On 28 April, journalist Matt Laslo asked him:

“Hey, what’s this we hear from Congressman Burlison—that you were in a UFO or UAP briefing you had asked to attend?”

Scalise replied:

“Well, we had a classified briefing that some of us went to.”

Laslo asked:

“Was it eye-opening for you?”

Scalise said:

“Well, you know, whenever you go to a briefing like that, there are some things you see that are eye-opening—and that’s about as far as I’ll go.”

Liberation Times has requested comment from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and the Department of War.

item.description: NASA has pushed back after reports claimed Administrator Jared Isaacman revealed that NASA possesses images of unexplained objects, telling Liberation Times that he was speaking generally about military sensors, satellites and other cameras.
item.content:encoded:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 11 July 2026

NASA has pushed back after reports claimed Administrator Jared Isaacman revealed that NASA possesses images of unexplained objects, telling Liberation Times that he was speaking generally about military sensors, satellites and other cameras.

The clarification follows headlines from outlets portraying Isaacman’s recent comments as an admission that NASA itself had photographed unidentified objects.

The NASA administrator told podcast host Jack Gordon:

“We have captured imagery, and this is what President Trump is very forward-leaning about, that based on the data that we have within that imagery, we don't know what it is.”

However, in a statement provided to Liberation Times, NASA said Isaacman was employing the “royal we” and was not specifically referring to imagery collected by the civilian space agency.

A NASA spokesperson stated:

“In the full context of the interview, which you can listen to online, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman specifically states he has seen no evidence of things like UFOs.

“Later, he speaks generally about the myriad of ways the ‘royal we’ can/have captured Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon imagery, including from military sensors and other satellites out there, but not specifically saying these are things NASA has captured. And finally, in that context, he is talking about weird angles and sun reflections in imagery that is unexplained.”

During the wide-ranging discussion with Gordon on 30 June 2026, Isaacman added:

“I think there's a very real possibility we're going to arrive at a conclusion in our lifetime that perhaps there's life everywhere out there and that it isn't as infrequent as we might think it to possibly be.”

Isaacman also suggested that NASA may already have the proof in its possession, but that evidence is currently stuck on Mars.

He stated:

“We got samples on Mars right now. If we bring them back, there is a very high probability that they will point to, at some point, microbial life at least on Mars.”  

The latest statements from Isaacman and NASA come amid new allegations concerning the Moon.

In a recent interview, Lue Elizondo, who previously led a Pentagon investigation into Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) known as the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, stated: 

“There are also photographs that I don't believe have been made public yet that show, on the lunar surface, what appear to be large monolithic structures with right-angle cuts.”

Elizondo added:

“I believe those photographs, if they have not been released yet, may be released soon. But they are certainly very intriguing looking at these objects from space.”

Elizondo previously worked for To The Stars Academy, a UAP organisation founded by musician Tom DeLonge.

DeLonge has claimed that, while developing the initiative, he presented his UFO-related project to senior NASA figures and was subsequently directed to a meeting at NASA’s Ames Research Center.

According to DeLonge, the individual he met at Ames repeatedly described himself as a sceptic before eventually instructing an associate to “introduce him to the general.”

DeLonge said he was placed in contact with the general within hours and later credited that figure with helping him assemble an advisory group drawn from the space, intelligence and defence communities.

The general is understood to be retired U.S. Air Force General William ‘Neil’ McCasland, former commander of the Air Force Research Laboratory, who has been missing since leaving his Albuquerque home on 27 February 2026.

The fourth tranche of UAP files released yesterday by the Department of War included three NASA images that appeared to show a rotating triangular object in Earth’s orbit.

The accompanying commentary noted: 

'During STS-80, between November 19 and December 7, 1996, astronauts aboard Space Shuttle Columbia captured a series of three images of an unidentified object in low-Earth orbit. In the second photograph, the object is visible near the center of the frame, to the right of the limb of the Earth. It appears to have rotated or tumbled about its major axis, which is consistent with the behavior of a free-floating object.' 

The release also comes amid unresolved questions over how anomalous detections in space are handled and who ultimately controls the resulting data. 

As previously reported by Liberation Times, veteran space operator Jim Shell has alleged - with what he described as medium confidence - that a concealed security control system within the US national-security space enterprise may be connected to UAP activity, potentially allowing anomalous orbital detections to be removed from standard catalogues before reaching operational commanders. 

Shell alleged that the system was obstructing routine tracking of objects in orbit, and, in some cases, diverting data away from the very commands responsible for defending the nation.
